Dock doors are closed, the yard is secured, and only count teams and the managers in charge remain on the floor.

3. The stocktake date is set by the warehouse manager. It falls outside regular Monday to Friday shifts 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 or is run as an approved shutdown with overtime. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime and attendance for the stocktake, and only rostered staff attend.

4. Stock controllers prepare and run the count. The two stock controllers freeze system stock, release wall-to-wall count tasks by WMS scanner, allocate count pairs by zone and location, and collect first counts, second counts and adjustment proposals. The shift supervisor on duty enforces zone discipline, PPE and freeze rules on the floor.

5. Every count runs as a WMS scanner task under personal login. Counters use the shared pool of 20 handheld scanners, follow the task by client, article, quantity, location, batch and date marks, and confirm each location by scan. Paper tallies, memory checks and free-looking estimates are not counts, and forced confirms without scanning physical stock are forbidden.

6. Count teams work in pairs and areas are counted once, independently. The first count records physical quantity against system at each location. Cold goods in Zone E are counted promptly so the +2 °C to +6 °C chain is not broken, doors kept closed, and hazmat in the cage is counted only under PR-13 without moving pallets between positions.

7. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Every location where first count and system differ is recounted by a second person on a fresh scanner task, without seeing the first result. If second count matches system, the first count is a count error. If it confirms the first count, a real discrepancy is logged for investigation.

8. Discrepancies are investigated before any adjustment. Open put-away tasks, unfinished replenishment, packing or staging moves, returns in Zone F awaiting decision, and quarantine transfers made the same day goods were found are checked. Damaged and quarantined stock is never counted as available, and write-off rules apply: the shift supervisor approves up to and including 750 EUR, the warehouse manager approves anything above 750 EUR per case.

9. Every count, recount and proposal is recorded in the WMS with user, time, zone, location, client, article and quantities. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory, trucks keep to 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings, and any injury, spill, rack impact or scanner fault is reported at once to the supervisor in charge.

10. No stocktake result becomes final until the warehouse manager has reviewed and signed it off. The manager reviews all second counts, investigations and proposed adjustments, approves corrections to system stock, and signs the wall-to-wall result as the new opening stock. Only after that sign-off are Zones A to F released back to receiving, put-away, replenishment, picking and dispatch.

title: Racking care and stock accuracy
text:
1. Stock on the rack is stock in the system. Zone B bulk racking with 2,400 pallet positions, block-stacking areas, pick faces in Zone C, cold positions in Zone E and quarantine and the 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F are only correct when every pallet sits on its WMS-assigned position and every move is scan-confirmed. A pallet on a free-looking bay is a stock error.

2. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg in total, including pallets and load. Every pallet with load may weigh at most 900 kg. No bay is loaded above 2,700 kg even if positions remain free, and free block-stacking outside the racking is limited to 3 pallets high and 3.5 m total height measured from the floor.

3. Storage positions are assigned only by WMS scanner task under PR-02 Put-away to storage and PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Operators place each booked pallet only to the position shown and confirm by scan under personal login from the shared pool of 20 scanners. No pallet is moved between bays, faces or zones without a task.

4. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy day to day. The two stock controllers run daily cycle counts on the rotating zone schedule, carry out recounts, investigate differences and prepare adjustments under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Inbound, picking, packing, dispatch and returns staff keep counted areas stable while a count is open.

5. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Any difference between first count and system is recounted by a second person on a fresh task without seeing the first result. If the second count matches system, the first count was an error. Only a confirmed discrepancy is investigated and proposed for sign-off.

6. Quarantined, held and unbooked goods are never counted as available. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09, returns await supervisor decision under PR-07, and uninspected goods stay in Zone A. Blocked quantities are logged separately and write-off rules apply: the shift supervisor approves up to and including 750 EUR, the warehouse manager approves above 750 EUR per case.

7. Racking condition is part of stock safety. Any impact, bent beam, missing pin, cracked frame, leaning pallet, leaking goods or blocked sprinkler or hydrant in any zone is reported at once to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. The bay is blocked, marked out of use and stays empty until repaired and released.

8. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician inspects all racking in Zone B, flow racks in Zone C, cold racking in Zone E and control racking in Zone F, logs beam, frame, anchor and labelling condition, and records every repair in the maintenance log. Damaged bays remain blocked and are excluded from put-away tasks until signed back into use.

9. Aisle, speed and PPE discipline protect racking and stock. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide with yellow barriers. The limit is 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings, aisle entries and junctions. High-visibility vests and class S3 footwear are mandatory, and only operators authorised by the warehouse manager drive forklifts and reach trucks.

10. Racking faults, blocked bays and open adjustments hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Impacts on the shift, bays blocked or released, monthly inspection findings, locations awaiting second count and adjustments awaiting sign-off are logged with zone, location, client and quantity. The incoming shift stores only to released positions and adjusts only after a second count, with annual results final only on warehouse-manager sign-off.

title: Returns acceptance and inspection
text:
1. Returns are accepted only in Zone F under PR-07 Returns handling. No return is received at doors 5-8, stored in Zone B, placed into a pick face in Zone C, or staged in Zone D. Every returning vehicle is handled through the dispatcher-assigned door and directed to Zone F control.

2. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery only. The delivery date and seal record from PR-06 Outbound dispatch are checked against the return note on arrival. Goods returned after 14 days, goods without delivery reference, or goods from another supplier are not accepted and are refused at the gate by the dispatcher.

3. Acceptance starts with document and identity check. Returns and packing staff compare carrier documents, client, order, article, quantity and reason for return with the WMS dispatch record. If documents are missing, differ from the booking, or show mixing of clients, acceptance is held and the shift supervisor and dispatcher are informed before unloading.

4. Unloading of accepted returns is carried out by instructed staff with suitable equipment only. Counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, electric and hand pallet jacks are used according to authorisation and capacity, with every pallet with load at most 900 kg observed. Speed limits of 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at ramps and crossings apply throughout.

5. Every returned unit is inspected in Zone F, without exception. Returns and packing staff open, count and check each carton and unit for condition, packaging integrity, labelling, batch and best-before date, cleanliness, leakage, damage and temperature status for chilled goods. Sampling, spot checks and paper-only acceptance are forbidden.

6. Inspection results are segregated immediately inside Zone F. Sound goods awaiting decision are staged in the marked returns inspection field, clearly separated by client and return. Damaged, suspect, leaking, temperature-failed or unidentifiable goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and are never held as available stock.

7. Hazmat and cold-chain returns follow special control. Hazmat items are handled only under PR-13 and stored only in the separate ventilated 60 m2 cage within the 3,000 kg site limit, never in general Zone F. Chilled returns are checked promptly under PR-12 Cold-chain handling so the +2 °C to +6 °C chain is verified, and goods outside acceptable condition are quarantined.

8. Every acceptance and inspection is recorded by scanner and log under PR-07. Return reference, date, client, article, quantities received, quantities passed, held and quarantined, batch and date marks, and inspector login from the shared pool of 20 handheld scanners are entered in the WMS. Findings, shortages and damage are reported at once to the shift supervisor.

9. No return re-enters stock at inspection. Inspected returns remain blocked in Zone F until the final disposition is decided under ops.ch09.s2. Restock, rework or scrap is proposed by returns and packing staff, but only the shift supervisor approves the final disposition. No adjustment is posted without a second count under PR-08.

10. Open returns hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Vehicles still at the door, pallets still to unload, units still to inspect, quarantine transfers completed or pending, and any spill, damage or incident on the shift are logged with door, client, article and quantity. The incoming shift continues only from open tasks in Zone F, with the same rule: no inspection of every unit, no decision.

title: Restock, rework or scrap decisions
text:
1. No inspected return leaves Zone F without a decided disposition. Every unit inspected under PR-07 Returns handling ends as restock to available stock, rework in Zone F, or scrap with write-off. Returns and packing staff propose the disposition, but only the shift supervisor approves the final disposition.

2. Proposals are made separately by client, article and return quantity. Returns staff record condition, packaging, labelling, batch and best-before date, and temperature status for chilled goods, and mark each line as proposed restock, proposed rework or proposed scrap. Mixed lines are split before proposal so no decision covers sound and damaged units together.

3. Restock is approved only for fully sound goods. Units must be unopened or intact, clean, correctly labelled, within date, with verified batch identity, and for chilled goods within +2 °C to +6 °C condition under PR-12. Anything damaged, soiled, leaking, relabelled by hand, out of date or temperature-failed is never approved for restock.

4. Restocked goods re-enter stock only by WMS scanner task under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. The shift supervisor releases the quantity, stock controllers confirm by second count where system quantity changes, and operators place to Zone B, Zone E or Zone C feed only by task. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count.

5. Rework is approved for goods that can be made sound in Zone F. This covers repacking into sound cartons, relabelling to WMS identity, rewrapping, and client-approved sets or kitting at the value-added stations. Rework is done only by instructed returns and packing staff, and reworked units are reinspected unit by unit before any restock decision.

6. Scrap is approved for goods that cannot be restocked or reworked. Damaged, contaminated, leaking, unidentifiable, out-of-date or quarantined goods go to scrap, are removed from available stock, and are held segregated in quarantine until collection or destruction. Quarantined goods are never picked, packed or dispatched.

7. Write-off approvals follow value per case. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 750 EUR. Any write-off above 750 EUR is reserved to the warehouse manager. No scrap is removed from stock or written off in value without one of these written approvals, and cases are never split to stay below the threshold.

8. Hazmat and cold-chain dispositions follow special control. Hazmat proposed for restock, rework or scrap is handled only under PR-13 in the ventilated 60 m2 cage within the 3,000 kg limit, with incompatible goods kept apart. Chilled goods outside acceptable condition go to quarantine the same day under PR-09 and are never reworked into available cold stock.

9. Every decision is recorded and traceable. Proposal, decision, approver, time, client, article, quantities for restock, rework and scrap, write-off value and approval reference, and scanner user from the shared pool of 20 handheld scanners are logged in the WMS under PR-07 and PR-09. Damaged goods found during inspection go to quarantine the same day they are found.

10. Open dispositions hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Lines awaiting supervisor decision, rework in progress in Zone F, scrap awaiting manager sign-off above 750 EUR, and restock tasks still to be put away are logged with client, article, quantity and location. The incoming shift continues only from open tasks and signed decisions, with the same rule: no approval, no restock, no rework release and no scrap.

title: Damaged goods and quarantine
text:
1. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, without exception. Any leaking, crushed, broken, soiled, contaminated, temperature-failed or otherwise suspect pallet, carton or unit found in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D, Zone E or the yard is taken out of use at once and transferred to quarantine under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

2. The finder never decides availability. Inbound operators, pickers, packing staff, forklift operators and dispatchers who find damage stop handling the goods, keep them segregated where found, and report at once to the shift supervisor. Only the supervisor directs the quarantine transfer, and quarantined goods are never picked, packed, replenished, staged or loaded.

3. Transfer to quarantine runs by WMS scanner task. Returns and packing staff or instructed operators move the goods to the marked quarantine field in Zone F, label them with client, article, quantity, date, finder and reason, and confirm the move by scan under personal login from the shared pool of 20 handheld scanners. Unlabelled quarantine stock is forbidden.

4. Quarantine in Zone F holds damaged and blocked goods only. Sound available stock, returns awaiting inspection and value-added packing are kept in separate marked fields and never mixed with quarantine. Quarantined pallets are placed stably within the footprint, with every pallet with load at most 900 kg, and leaking goods are contained and reported immediately.

5. Special goods follow special control inside quarantine. Hazmat items go only to the separate ventilated 60 m2 cage under PR-13 within the 3,000 kg site limit, never to general quarantine. Chilled goods outside +2 °C to +6 °C condition go to quarantine the same day under PR-12 and are never returned to Zone E or fed to chilled pick faces.

6. Quarantine quantities are blocked in the system. Damaged goods are never booked or counted as available stock, and any system quantity change requires a second count under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Stock controllers carry out the recount independently, and no adjustment is ever posted without a second count.

7. Every quarantine case ends in a written disposition. Returns and packing staff record condition and propose restock after rework, rework in Zone F, or scrap, and the shift supervisor approves the final disposition. Goods that cannot be made fully sound are scrapped, held segregated in quarantine until collection or destruction, and never re-enter stock.

8. Write-off approvals follow value per case. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 750 EUR. Any write-off above 750 EUR is reserved to the warehouse manager. No scrap is removed from stock or written off in value without one of these written approvals, and cases are never split to stay below the threshold.

9. Spills, injuries and rack damage linked to damaged goods are handled at once. The shift supervisor secures the area, calls the maintenance technician for racking or equipment damage, ensures spill containment under PR-13, and records the incident for review. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory, and trucks keep to 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings.

10. Open quarantine cases hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Transfers completed or still to move, quarantine quantity by client and location, dispositions awaiting decision, scrap awaiting sign-off above 750 EUR, and any spill or incident are logged with client, article, quantity and location. The incoming shift continues only from open tasks and signed decisions.

title: Aisles, walkways and speed limits
text:
1. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and run through the hall past Zones A to F to the dock doors. They carry counterbalance forklifts, pallet jacks and through traffic only. They are marked on the floor, kept fully passable, and never used for staging, parking, charging or waste.

2. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide and serve the high-bay racking in Zone B and the flow racks and pick faces in Zone C. They are used by reach trucks and feed moves under scanner task only. No pallet, wrapper foil, scanner trolley or waste is placed or staged in a rack aisle.

3. Pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and physically separated by yellow barriers along their full length. They lead through the hall, to Zone F, to the office annex and to the marked crossings. Walkways are for people on foot only and are never blocked, narrowed or driven on.

4. Pedestrians use only walkways and marked crossings. Cutting across a 4.0 m transport aisle, a 3.0 m storage aisle, a dock approach or Zone D staging outside a crossing is forbidden. Where a walkway meets a driving aisle, pedestrians cross only at the marked crossing with full visibility.

5. The speed limit inside the building is 8 km/h. It applies to every counterbalance forklift, reach truck, electric pallet jack and hand pallet jack in the hall, in all zones and in all aisles. It is enforced by the shift supervisor on shift and applies on both shifts and on any approved Saturday overtime.

6. The speed limit in the fenced yard is 12 km/h. It applies from the gate to the manoeuvring area, the driver waiting area and the approaches to all 8 dock doors. Engines are switched off while waiting, and manoeuvring takes place only in the marked area at walking pace on approach to the 1.2 m ramps.

7. The limit is 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet. This covers all marked pedestrian zones, walkway crossings, aisle entries and junctions, dock ramps at doors 1-8, Zone A inspection space and Zone D staging fronts. Trucks slow to 5 km/h before the point, give way, and stop if a pedestrian is in the zone.

8. Pedestrians always have priority. Drivers stop at crossings, at barrier openings and at blind junctions, make eye contact where possible, and proceed only when the way is clear. Horns are used as warning at junctions and ramp entries, not as right of way. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.

9. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory on all aisles and walkways in the hall. Barriers, floor markings, mirrors and signs are safety equipment and must not be moved, covered or removed. Any damaged barrier, faded marking or blind spot is reported at once to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician.

10. Blocked or unsafe aisles stop driving work. If a 4.0 m aisle, 3.0 m aisle, walkway or crossing is blocked by pallets, equipment or spill, operators stop, secure the area and report to the shift supervisor, who has the route cleared before work resumes. Open blockages, speed violations and near misses are logged and handed over at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

title: Yard, docks and ramps
text:
1. The fenced yard outside the hall covers about 3,500 m2 and holds all vehicle movement for the site. It contains the approaches to all 8 dock doors, the marked manoeuvring area for trailers and vans, and the marked driver waiting area. No warehousing, staging or picking takes place in the yard.

2. Dock doors have fixed directions that are never interchanged. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and serve Zone A receiving. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and serve Zone D dispatch. No inbound truck docks at doors 5-8, and no outbound truck docks at doors 1-4, even if a door appears free.

3. No truck enters a ramp or docks without a dispatcher assignment. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling, books every carrier in advance, and assigns a fixed door and time slot with carrier name, vehicle identification and expected pallet count. Unbooked, early or late arrivals wait for dispatcher replanning and are never waved to a door from the floor.

4. Drivers report on arrival to the marked driver waiting area, secure the vehicle and remain there until called forward in slot order. Drivers never enter the hall, Zone A, Zone D or the dock approaches on foot, and never operate levellers, wrappers or handling equipment. Escorted access is only with full PPE: high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear.

5. Yard traffic is separated from people by layout and speed. The speed limit in the yard is 12 km/h, reduced to 5 km/h at all dock ramps, at crossings, at barrier openings and wherever people and trucks meet. Manoeuvring takes place only in the marked manoeuvring area, reversing is guided where visibility is limited, and engines are switched off while waiting and at the door.

6. Each of the 8 dock doors has its own leveller at 1.2 m dock height. The driver positions to the assigned door only when released by the dispatcher, brakes and secures the vehicle against movement, opens curtains or rear doors, and returns to the safe position. Inbound operators then take the door from the Zone A side, outbound operators from the Zone D side.

7. Levellers, doors and dock approaches are safety equipment and are kept clear and serviceable. No pallet, wrapper foil, baler waste, parked jack or waiting trailer blocks a door, leveller, emergency route or pedestrian barrier. A defective door, leveller, shelter or light is reported at once to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, and the door stays out of use until repaired and logged.

8. Pedestrian routes never cross open dock work. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers and the marked crossings to the office annex and waiting area. Cutting across manoeuvring areas, reversing trailers or the fronts of doors 1-8 is forbidden. Trucks give way at every crossing and stop if a pedestrian is in the ramp zone.

9. Yard and ramp work takes place only inside operating hours, Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus approved Saturday morning overtime. Outside these hours dock doors are closed, levellers parked, and the yard secured. Trucks arriving outside staffed hours wait outside the schedule and are not positioned, loaded or unloaded until the next assigned slot.

10. Open doors, waiting trucks and ramp faults hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Trucks on ramps at doors 1-8, vehicles held in the waiting area, missed slots, blocked doors and any yard incident, near miss or equipment defect are logged with door, carrier, time and quantity. The incoming shift works only dispatcher-assigned doors, with the same rule: no assignment, no docking.

title: Pedestrian protection and PPE
text:
1. No person enters or remains on the warehouse floor without full pedestrian protection. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone in the hall at all times, with no exceptions for staff, managers, drivers or visitors. Anyone without correct vest and footwear is refused access and reports to the shift supervisor.

2. High-visibility vests are worn closed and kept visible over all other clothing. Jackets, bags, scarves or loads carried in front must not cover the reflective strips while on the floor. Class S3 footwear is laced or fastened correctly, with toe caps, puncture plates and closed uppers intact. Damaged, open or makeshift footwear is not permitted in any zone.

3. Forklift and reach-truck operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving as part of pedestrian protection. The belt is fastened before driving off and remains fastened until the truck is parked with brake applied. No truck is driven with a missing or defective belt, and the defect is reported at once to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician.

4. Pedestrians move only inside physical protection. All pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and physically separated by yellow barriers along their full length. Walkways lead through the hall past Zones A to F, to Zone F control, to the office annex and to the marked crossings. They are for people on foot only and are never driven on, narrowed or used for staging.

5. Pedestrians cross driving areas only at marked crossings. Cutting across a 4.0 m main transport aisle, a 3.0 m rack storage aisle, a dock approach at doors 1-8, Zone A inspection space or Zone D staging outside a crossing is forbidden. At crossings pedestrians stop at the barrier opening, check both directions, establish eye contact with the driver where possible, and cross only when trucks have stopped.

6. Barriers, markings, mirrors and signs are safety equipment under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Yellow barriers, floor lines, crossing marks, pedestrian symbols and blind-junction mirrors must not be moved, covered, leaned on with pallets or removed. Any bent barrier, faded marking, broken light or blind spot is reported at once to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician and logged for repair.

7. Pedestrians always have priority over trucks. At walkway crossings, aisle entries and junctions, dock ramps, and all marked pedestrian zones, trucks slow to 5 km/h before the point, give way and stop if a pedestrian is in the zone. Drivers sound the horn as warning at junctions and ramp entries, never as a claim of right of way. Inside the building the general limit is 8 km/h and in the yard 12 km/h, always reduced to 5 km/h where people and trucks meet.

8. Drivers, visitors and other non-warehouse staff remain pedestrians under escort. They wait in the marked driver waiting area in the fenced yard and never enter the hall, Zone A, Zone D or dock approaches on foot unless escorted and wearing full PPE. They never operate levellers, forklifts, pallet jacks, wrappers or the baler, and never walk through manoeuvring areas or behind reversing trailers.

9. Cold, control and packing areas keep the same protection. In Zone E staff wear provided cold-protection clothing over the mandatory vest and footwear and limit dwell time to the scanner task. In Zone F, at packing stations, wrappers and the baler, and in the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage surround, walkways, barriers and 5 km/h meeting-point discipline apply unchanged, with spills, strapping, foil and cardboard cleared immediately as trip and slip hazards.

10. Every pedestrian near miss, barrier impact, PPE refusal, spill or blind-spot finding is reported immediately to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. The supervisor stops unsafe work, secures the area, has the route or barrier restored, and ensures the event is recorded and reviewed. Open defects, violations and follow-up actions hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and instructions on PPE, walkways and priority are binding on all persons on site.

title: Electric fleet overview
text:
1. Our materials-handling fleet is fully electric and covers all moves from Zone A to Zone D. It consists of 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks. No diesel, gas or other powered trucks are used on site.

2. The 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t handle general work across the hall. They support unloading in Zone A, put-away to Zone B, Zone E and Zone F, replenishment feed to Zone C, and staging and loading in Zone D. They run on the 4.0 m main transport aisles and never enter the 3.0 m high-bay aisles for high lifting.

3. The 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t work the high bays in Zone B. They retrieve and place reserve pallets in the high-bay racking with 2,400 positions under WMS scanner task only. They operate in the 3.0 m rack storage aisles and at the feed points to Zone C. They are never used for dock loading or yard work.

4. The 11 electric pallet jacks handle horizontal moves and forward fill. They move booked pallets in Zone A inspection space, small replenishment lots in Zone C, packed pallets to the wrappers, and staged pallets in Zone D. They are used only within their rated capacity and with the 900 kg pallet limit observed.

5. The 12 hand pallet jacks cover small moves only. They are used at packing stations, at the Zone A booking area, in Zone F control fields and for short repositioning in Zone D. They are never used to replace a forklift for heavy, high or long-distance moves, and never loaded above capacity.

6. Dispatch operates 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers for outbound pallets. Every pallet for Zone D is wrapped on one of these wrappers after packing and labelling under PR-05 Packing and labelling. Loose, torn or half-wrapped pallets are rewrapped. Only instructed staff operate the wrappers with guards in place.

7. Packing operates 1 cardboard baler for packaging waste. Flattened cartons, dividers and paper from packing and Zone F are fed to the baler continuously so stations, wrappers, aisles and dock approaches stay clear. The baler is operated only by instructed staff, and any fault is reported at once.

8. Each of the 8 dock doors has its own leveller at 1.2 m dock height. Inbound doors 1-4 serve Zone A, outbound doors 5-8 serve Zone D. Levellers, doors, shelters and lights are safety equipment, kept clear and serviceable, and a defective door stays out of use until repaired and logged by the maintenance technician.

9. Teams share 20 handheld WMS scanners for all tasks. Put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03, picking under PR-04, packing, staging and loading under PR-05 and PR-06, counts under PR-08 and quarantine moves under PR-09 all run by scanner task under personal login. Scanners are returned, charged and handed over between shifts.

10. Fleet size fixes availability on every shift. With two shifts 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 plus approved Saturday overtime, the shift supervisor allocates the 9 forklifts, 5 reach trucks, 11 electric jacks, 12 hand jacks, 2 wrappers and 20 scanners to zones and tasks. Trucks with defects, including defective seat belts, are parked, marked and reported, and handover at 14:00 under PR-15 logs trucks in use, trucks out of use and wrapper or baler faults.

title: Authorisation and daily checks
text:
1. No licence, no truck. No employee drives a counterbalance forklift or a reach truck at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. without personal authorisation by the warehouse manager. Training elsewhere, experience with pallet jacks or instruction for wrappers and the baler is not an authorisation to drive.

2. Authorisation is personal, equipment-specific and recorded. The warehouse manager authorises each new forklift and reach-truck operator by name for counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, for reach trucks rated at 2.0 t, or for both. The authorisation list is kept current, and the shift supervisor checks it before allocating drivers on the shift.

3. Electric pallet jacks, hand pallet jacks, stretch wrappers and the cardboard baler require instruction, not manager authorisation. No employee uses an electric pallet jack, hand pallet jack, semi-automatic wrapper or baler without instruction for that equipment. Forklifts and reach trucks additionally require the manager authorisation in items 1-2.

4. Every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day. This covers all 9 counterbalance forklifts, 5 reach trucks and 11 electric pallet jacks in service that day. Hand pallet jacks are visually checked before use. A truck without a completed daily check for that day is not driven.

5. The daily check is carried out by the designated operator under personal login and covers brakes, steering, horn, lights, hydraulics, forks, wheels, battery charge and condition, and seat belt on forklifts and reach trucks. Findings are entered on the daily check record with truck number, date, time and operator signature. The 20 shared WMS scanners do not replace this paper or terminal record.

6. Any defect stops the truck. Trucks with defective brakes, steering, lights, hydraulics, forks, wheels, battery faults or missing or defective seat belts are parked safely, marked out of use with the key removed, and reported at once to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. They are not driven, jump-started or worked around until repaired and released.

7. The maintenance technician owns trucks, racking and dock equipment and logs every repair. Faults from daily checks, shift reports and handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover are entered in the maintenance log with truck, fault, action and release. Only the technician releases a repaired truck back to service, and the next daily check starts the cycle again.

8. The shift supervisor on shift enforces the check discipline on the floor under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. The supervisor verifies that daily checks are complete before allocating the 9 forklifts, 5 reach trucks and 11 electric jacks to Zone A, B, C, D, E and F tasks, stops any unchecked or defective truck, and ensures replacements come only from checked, authorised capacity.

9. Authorisation can be suspended immediately. Unsafe driving, speeding above 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard or 5 km/h at meeting points, driving without seat belt fastened, carrying pedestrians, or driving an unchecked or defective truck leads to instant removal from driving by the shift supervisor. Return to driving requires review and renewed authorisation by the warehouse manager.

10. Checks and authorisations hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15. Trucks checked and in use, trucks out of use with fault reference, authorisations granted, suspended or pending, and any incident, near miss or rack impact involving a truck are logged with truck number, operator and zone. The incoming shift starts only with authorised operators on checked trucks, with the same rule: no authorisation, no driving, and no documented check, no first use.

title: Safe operation rules
text:
1. Only authorised operators drive powered trucks under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t and reach trucks rated at 2.0 t are driven only with personal authorisation by the warehouse manager. Electric pallet jacks are driven only after instruction, and hand pallet jacks are used only for small moves within capacity.

2. Forklift and reach-truck operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. The belt is fastened before driving off, stays fastened during the whole run, and is released only after the truck is parked with brake applied. No truck is driven with a missing or defective belt.

3. Speed limits apply to every move and are enforced by the shift supervisor. The limit is 8 km/h inside the building and 12 km/h in the fenced yard, reduced to 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including marked pedestrian zones, walkway crossings, aisle entries and junctions, and the dock ramps at doors 1-8.

4. Trucks keep to the marked driving routes. Counterbalance forklifts and pallet jacks run on the 4.0 m main transport aisles and zone approaches. Reach trucks work the 3.0 m rack storage aisles in Zone B and the feed points to Zone C. Pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m with yellow barriers are never driven on, narrowed or blocked.

5. Loads are carried safely within limits. Every pallet with load may weigh at most 900 kg, loads sit stably within the pallet footprint without overhang, forks stay low during travel with the mast tilted back, and high lifting takes place only in the high bays with the reach truck under WMS scanner task. Overweight, leaning, damaged or leaking pallets are not carried until repacked.

6. Pedestrians always have priority under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. At crossings, barrier openings, blind junctions and ramp entries drivers slow to 5 km/h, give way, stop if a pedestrian is in the zone, and sound the horn as warning. Pedestrians are never carried on forks, on pallets or on the truck steps.

7. Dock, leveller and ramp work follows dispatcher assignment only. Trucks approach doors 1-4 inbound and doors 5-8 outbound at 5 km/h at the ramp, stop square to the 1.2 m leveller, and handle only the released load from the Zone A or Zone D side. Manoeuvring in the yard is at walking pace on approach, with engines off while waiting.

8. Parking, charging and visibility discipline is binding. Trucks are parked only in marked areas with forks lowered, brake applied and key removed, electric trucks are charged only at the marked charge points, and lights are used in dim areas and at ramps. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory, and loads, doors and racking must never block the driver's view.

9. Every truck must have its documented check before first use each day. A truck with defective brakes, steering, horn, lights, hydraulics, forks, wheels, battery or seat belt is parked, marked out of use and reported at once to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. Any speeding, near miss, rack impact, spill or injury stops work and is recorded for review.

10. Trucks in use, faults and violations hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Operators, truck numbers, zones, daily checks completed, trucks out of use with fault references, and any incident, speed or belt violation on the shift are logged. The incoming shift starts only with authorised operators on checked trucks, with the same rule: belt on, speed observed, no check no drive.

title: Evacuation and drills
text:
1. Evacuation follows PR-14 Emergency evacuation on every shift and on any approved Saturday morning overtime. Alarms, escape routes, assembly discipline and roll call apply equally in Zones A to F, in the office annex and in the fenced yard. No work priority overrides an evacuation order.

2. Any person discovering fire, smoke, gas leak, structural damage, major spill or other immediate danger raises the alarm at once and reports to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. The shift supervisor takes charge of incident response, stops all driving and handling work, and orders evacuation of the hall where required.

3. On evacuation all staff leave the warehouse hall immediately by the nearest marked escape route. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack storage aisles of 3.0 m and pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m with yellow barriers lead to the exits, and emergency routes, doors and zone boundaries are kept clear at all times so escape is never blocked by pallets, equipment or waste.

4. Trucks are stopped safely where they stand with brakes applied, dock work is interrupted, and levellers, wrappers and the baler are left in safe state. Forklift operators park with forks lowered only if this does not delay escape, otherwise they leave the truck and walk out. No one returns for scanners, paperwork or personal items.

5. Everyone assembles at the assembly point by the north fence in the fenced yard. Pedestrians use only the marked walkways and crossings to reach it, keeping clear of manoeuvring trailers, dock ramps and the hall exits. Drivers in the marked waiting area join the assembly point and remain under the shift supervisor's direction.

6. Roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building. The shift supervisor checks all floor staff, dispatchers, maintenance, floaters and escorted visitors against the shift roster, including the outgoing and incoming teams around the 14:00 handover. Missing persons are reported at once to the emergency services and no search is made inside by staff.

7. Re-entry is forbidden until formally released. Only the shift supervisor, after clearance by the fire service or by the warehouse manager, authorises return to the hall. The roll call must be complete and the cause resolved before any put-away, replenishment, picking, packing or loading resumes at doors 1-8.

8. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14. The drill covers alarm raising, escape by marked routes, shutdown of trucks and dock doors, assembly by the north fence and full roll call. It is held across shifts so morning staff 06:00-14:00 and afternoon staff 14:00-22:00 are both exercised during the year.

9. The shift supervisor runs the drill on the floor and the warehouse manager owns the drill programme for the site. Attendance, alarm time, escape time, roll-call result and defects in routes, barriers, markings, lights or doors are recorded, and every incident report from a drill is reviewed by the shift supervisor with follow-up assigned to the maintenance technician or stock controllers concerned.

10. Defects and open follow-up hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Drill dates completed, next quarterly drill due, blocked escape routes, faulty alarms, barrier or marking damage, and any evacuation or alarm event on the shift are logged with zone, time and action owner. The incoming shift starts with clear escape routes and a known assembly state, with the same rule: roll call at the north fence before re-entry.

title: Safety inspections and incidents
text:
1. Safety on site is controlled by documented inspections and by immediate reporting of every incident. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month, and every injury, near miss, spill, alarm, rack impact or equipment fault is reported at once to the shift supervisor on shift, who secures the area and ensures the event is recorded.

2. The monthly racking inspection covers all racking in Zone B, flow racks in Zone C, cold racking in Zone E and control racking in Zone F. Beams, frames, anchors, pins, bracing, load signs, bay labels and sprinkler and hydrant clearance are checked bay by bay, including the 2,400 pallet positions in Zone B and the block-stacking fields.

3. The maintenance technician carries out the monthly inspection and logs every finding. Beam deflection, bent uprights, missing pins, cracked welds, loose anchors, leaning pallets above the 900 kg unit limit or above the 2,700 kg bay limit, and any overheight above 3.5 m in block stacks are recorded with zone, bay and date. Every repair is logged with action, parts and release date.

4. A damaged bay is blocked immediately and stays out of use. The shift supervisor marks the bay, removes it from WMS put-away tasks, and keeps pallets clear until the maintenance technician has repaired and released it. No pallet is placed to a free-looking but blocked bay to keep system stock correct.

5. Dock equipment, trucks and barriers are checked with the racking round. The 8 levellers at 1.2 m dock height, doors 1-8, shelters and lights, yellow barriers on the 1.2 m walkways, floor markings for 4.0 m transport aisles and 3.0 m storage aisles, mirrors and crossings are inspected for damage and function. Defects are logged for repair in the same maintenance log.

6. Any incident stops the unsafe work first. The finder stops handling, keeps goods or equipment where safe, and reports at once to the shift supervisor. The supervisor takes charge of incident response on the shift, gives first aid, contains spills under PR-13, closes aisles, ramps or bays as needed, and calls the maintenance technician where racking, trucks or dock equipment are involved.

7. Every incident is recorded the same shift under PR-10, PR-11 or PR-14 as applicable. Who, when, where, truck number or bay, client and quantity where goods are affected, PPE and speed compliance, witnesses and immediate action are logged with scanner user or supervisor signature. Reports cover injuries, near misses, spills, temperature alarms, barrier impacts, wrapper and baler faults and rack impacts.

8. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report from the supervisor's shift. Reports are checked for completeness, cause, damage to the 2,700 kg bays, 900 kg pallets or fleet of 9 forklifts, 5 reach trucks, 11 electric jacks and 12 hand jacks, and follow-up is assigned to the maintenance technician, stock controllers, returns staff or operators concerned and checked as carried out.

9. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory during all inspections and incident work, forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, and the limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps are enforced. Pedestrians always have priority and use only walkways and crossings to reach the affected area.

10. Inspections, incidents and open follow-up hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Last monthly inspection date and next due date, bays blocked or released, trucks out of use, incident reports raised and reviewed, and repairs or retraining still open are logged with zone, location and action owner. The incoming shift starts only with released bays and checked trucks, with the same rule: no repair release, no use.

title: Cold-chain and hazmat controls
text:
1. Zone E is held continuously between +2 °C and +6 °C under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. No other range applies. The 300 m2 chilled store holds only booked, temperature-fit goods released from Zone A, and no ambient, quarantine or hazmat stock is ever held there. The chain starts at inbound inspection and is never broken by waiting.

2. A manual temperature verification is carried out every shift in Zone E. The shift supervisor ensures the check is done on the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, and on any approved Saturday morning overtime when cold stock is held. Readings, time, measuring point and operator login are logged under PR-12.

3. Fixed high, low and door-open alarms monitor Zone E continuously. Any alarm is reported at once to the shift supervisor on shift, who keeps cold doors closed, secures the goods, stops picking, replenishment and dispatch of affected pallets, and calls the maintenance technician. Affected stock stays blocked until checked and released.

4. Cold doors, curtains and locks are kept closed except for immediate scanner-tasked moves. Doors are never propped open, pallets are never staged in the doorway or temperature lock, and no truck is parked there. Put-away from Zone A and replenishment to Zone C run in small, prompt moves, and goods outside acceptable condition go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

5. The ventilated hazmat cage inside Zone F is the only permitted place for hazmat under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. The cage measures 60 m2 and holds at most 3,000 kg in total at any time. Hazmat never sits in Zone A, B, C, D or E, not even briefly staged, and any item found outside is reported and moved at once.

6. Every pallet with load may weigh at most 900 kg, so the cage takes at most 3 full-weight pallets. Cage quantity is checked before every put-away by WMS scanner task under PR-02, and no pallet is released if current stock plus new weight would exceed 3,000 kg. The cage stays locked and ventilated, incompatible goods are kept apart, and access is limited to instructed staff.

7. Spill response starts with stop, secure and report. The finder stops work, leaves the spill untouched, warns others and reports at once to the shift supervisor. The supervisor closes the aisle, bay or ramp area, ensures ventilation and containment with the provided spill means under PR-13, and calls the maintenance technician where racking, trucks or dock equipment are affected.

8. Spills are cleared only with correct means and protection. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory, plus gloves, goggles and other spill-kit protection as directed by PR-13. Leaking, damaged or unlabelled hazmat is contained, never repacked in the aisle, and moved only as directed to the cage or quarantine. Contaminated absorbents go to segregated quarantine for disposal.

9. Every cold-chain check, alarm and hazmat event is recorded the same shift. Manual readings, alarm times, goods and client affected, cage quantity on hand, spill location, containment action, truck number or bay, witnesses and supervisor review are logged in the WMS with user login from the shared pool of 20 handheld scanners. Quarantine transfers, second counts under PR-08 and write-off approvals up to 750 EUR by the supervisor and above 750 EUR by the warehouse manager are attached.

10. Open controls hand over visibly at 14:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Last manual readings, open alarms, cold pallets still to move, cage quantity against the 3,000 kg and 3-pallet limits, open spills, blocked bays and repairs still pending are logged with zone, client, quantity and action owner. Trucks keep to 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings and ramps, and the incoming shift starts only with released positions and cleared routes.

title: End-of-shift handover
text:
1. Every shift ends with a formal handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover from the outgoing shift supervisor to the incoming shift supervisor at 14:00. The handover covers the whole floor, all open loads and all unresolved issues, so the next shift starts with a clear and safe picture. No shift is left without a supervisor in charge.

2. The handover takes place on the floor at 14:00, face to face. The morning shift 06:00-14:00 hands to the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, and the afternoon shift hands to the next morning shift by written log secured with the dock doors closed. On any approved Saturday morning overtime the same handover closes the session and returns the site to secured state.

3. Open dock doors and yard status are handed over first. Trucks on ramps at doors 1-4 inbound and doors 5-8 outbound, vehicles held in the marked driver waiting area, missed slots, blocked doors or levellers, and seal numbers issued are logged with door, carrier, time and quantity. The incoming shift works only dispatcher-assigned doors and slots.

4. Unfinished goods flow is handed over by zone and task. Booked pallets still in Zone A, held document or inspection cases, open put-away tasks to Zone B, Zone E and Zone F, faces still to replenish in Zone C, open picking and packing tasks, and staged, released and unreleased loads in Zone D are logged with client, order, quantity and location.

5. Controlled stock is handed over separately. Manual temperature readings and open alarms in Zone E between +2 °C and +6 °C, cage quantity on hand against the 3,000 kg and 3-pallet limits in the 60 m2 ventilated cage, quarantine quantity by client, returns awaiting inspection or supervisor decision, and rework or scrap awaiting sign-off are logged with zone and action owner.

6. Counts and accuracy status are handed over by the stock controllers through the supervisors. Locations counted and still to count in the daily rotation, locations awaiting second count, adjustments awaiting sign-off, and the rule that no adjustment is posted without a second count are confirmed. Write-offs up to 750 EUR await the shift supervisor, above 750 EUR the warehouse manager.

7. Equipment and racking status is handed over by number and bay. The 9 forklifts, 5 reach trucks, 11 electric jacks, 12 hand jacks, 2 wrappers, 1 baler and 20 scanners in use or out of use, daily checks completed, trucks blocked with fault references, and rack bays blocked after impact or monthly inspection are logged with truck number, bay and repair reference.

8. Safety events are handed over with review state. Every injury, near miss, spill, barrier impact, temperature alarm, speed or seat-belt violation, wrapper or baler fault and incident report raised on the shift is logged with time, zone, witnesses and immediate action. The outgoing supervisor confirms which reports are reviewed and which follow-up remains open for maintenance or retraining.

9. The handover is recorded and signed under personal login. The outgoing and incoming supervisors sign the PR-15 log with time, roster present including floaters, zones covered, and all open points above. Open scanner tasks stay open in the WMS, counted areas stay frozen until closed, and blocked bays, doors and trucks stay blocked until repaired and released.

10. The incoming shift starts only from the handover. Work continues only from open scanner tasks, released faces and positions, and dispatcher-assigned doors, with the same rules: no booking, no put-away, no replenishment, no picking without scan-verification, no unwrapped or unlabelled pallet to Zone D, and no release, no loading. If any point is unclear, work in that area stops until the supervisors clarify with the warehouse manager.

title: Speed limits and shared areas
text:
1. Pedestrian safety has priority over all vehicle movement in every shared area of the site. No time pressure, delivery slot or operational urgency justifies exceeding a speed limit or passing a pedestrian at unsafe distance.

2. All materials handling equipment, including counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks, electric pallet jacks and hand pallet jacks when towed or used in transport aisles, is subject to the speed limits in this section. The limits apply to all operators, including supervisors, maintenance staff and floaters, whenever they drive a truck.

3. Inside the warehouse hall the maximum speed is 8 km/h. This applies throughout Zones A to F, in the 4.0 m wide main transport aisles, in the 3.0 m wide rack storage aisles in Zone B, and in the picking, packing and staging areas in Zones C, D and F.

4. In the fenced yard of about 3,500 m2 the maximum speed is 12 km/h. This applies to all movements between the gate, the marked waiting area, the parking positions and dock doors 1-8, and to manoeuvring of trailers at the 1.2 m high docks.

5. Wherever people and trucks meet, the maximum speed is 5 km/h. These locations are signposted and marked on the floor and include all marked pedestrian zones, all marked pedestrian crossings, and the entrances to the 1.2 m wide physically separated pedestrian walkways protected by yellow barriers.

6. On and immediately in front of dock ramps and dock levellers the maximum speed is 5 km/h. Trucks shall approach the dock edge at walking pace, stop before the leveller edge, check that the leveller is correctly seated and the trailer is secured, and only then proceed to load or unload.

7. Pedestrians have the right of way at all marked crossings and in all marked pedestrian zones. The driver shall stop the truck, make eye contact or exchange a clear hand signal with the pedestrian, and only proceed when the crossing is fully clear.

8. Outside marked crossings, pedestrians shall use the separated 1.2 m wide walkways and shall not enter transport aisles or shared manoeuvring areas unless the task requires it. Drivers shall slow to 5 km/h, sound the horn at blind corners and rack intersections, and give way whenever a pedestrian is in or about to enter the travel path.

9. Reversing in shared areas is limited to the minimum necessary. The driver shall look in the direction of travel, use mirrors and any fitted warning devices, and stop immediately if a pedestrian or another truck enters the danger zone. A second person shall guide the manoeuvre where visibility is restricted, particularly at dock doors 1-8.

10. External drivers and visitors shall remain in the marked waiting area in the yard and shall never enter the hall or walk in transport or dock areas unaccompanied. Inbound operators and dispatchers shall collect them or call them forward only when the assigned door and time slot are ready.

11. Overtaking of another truck is prohibited in rack aisles, at crossings, in pedestrian zones and on dock ramps. In main aisles and in the yard, overtaking is permitted only with clear visibility, sufficient width and a maximum passing speed of 5 km/h relative to the pedestrian or vehicle being passed.

12. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor enforces these limits and priority rules on each shift. Any speeding, failure to give way, or unauthorised pedestrian presence in a truck area shall be stopped immediately, reported as an incident, and followed up under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

title: Walkways, aisles and dock areas
text:
1. People and trucks are kept apart by design. Pedestrians use only the marked, physically segregated system of walkways and crossings, and trucks use only the marked transport aisles, dock manoeuvring areas and yard routes. No storage, staging, charging or parking is permitted in either system.

2. All pedestrian walkways inside the hall are 1.2 m wide and are physically separated from vehicle areas by yellow barriers. The barriers shall remain continuous, upright and anchored. Any damage, displacement or missing section shall be reported to the shift supervisor immediately and the area secured until repaired.

3. Walkways serve all routes between the office annex, Zones A to F, welfare facilities, emergency exits and the yard gates. Pedestrians shall stay inside the barriers for the full length of the route and shall enter or leave a walkway only at a marked opening or marked pedestrian crossing.

4. Pedestrian crossings over transport aisles and over dock approach lanes are marked on the floor and signposted. Pedestrians shall cross only at these crossings. Pallets, wrap, waste and equipment shall never be placed on a walkway, opening or crossing, even briefly.

5. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. They provide two-way movement for counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks between Zones A, B, C, D, E and F and to the dock doors. The full width, including floor markings and the safety clearance to racks and barriers, shall be kept free of goods and obstructions.

6. Rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide. Only one truck shall operate in a rack aisle section with restricted visibility at a time. Drivers shall enter at walking pace, sound the horn before entry and at intersections, and keep to the centre where marked.

7. Dock areas are part of the truck system, not pedestrian areas. The staging areas in Zone A at doors 1-4 and in Zone D at doors 5-8, the dock levellers and the ramps immediately in front of the doors shall be kept clear except for the load being actively loaded or unloaded.

8. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and serve Zone A receiving. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and serve Zone D dispatch. No door shall be used in the opposite direction. The 1.2 m dock height edge shall be marked and fitted with protection, and the dock opening shall remain closed or guarded whenever no trailer is docked.

9. Every carrier is assigned a door and a time slot by the dispatcher. Drivers report to the marked waiting area in the fenced yard and wait there until called forward to the assigned door. Drivers shall never enter the hall, walk in transport or dock areas unaccompanied, or move between doors without dispatcher instruction.

10. Inbound operators at doors 1-4 and dispatchers at doors 5-8 call drivers forward only when the door, leveller and staging area are ready. Before loading or unloading, the truck shall confirm the trailer is correctly positioned, braked and secured at the leveller, the leveller is correctly seated, and all personnel are clear of the danger zone.

11. Floor markings, signs and barriers for walkways, aisles, crossings, waiting areas and dock doors shall be high-contrast and maintained. The maintenance technician restores faded or damaged markings and barriers, and the shift supervisor checks each shift that aisles, walkways and dock approaches are clear and passable.

12. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor enforces this segregation on each shift under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Any walking outside walkways, storage in aisles, use of a wrong dock door, or driver leaving the waiting area without authorisation shall be stopped and reported as an incident.

title: Driver authorisation and truck checks
text:
1. No person shall drive or operate any powered materials handling equipment on site without prior authorisation. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators, and no licence, no truck — without a valid licence or certificate and a written site authorisation, driving is prohibited.

2. Authorised drivers are the 8 appointed forklift operators. They are the only staff permitted to drive counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks. No picker, inbound operator, stock controller, dispatcher, floater, visitor or external driver shall drive a powered truck unless separately licensed and authorised in writing by the warehouse manager.

3. Authorisation is type-specific. A driver authorised only for electric pallet jacks shall not drive a counterbalance forklift or reach truck. Authorisation for the 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t and the 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t requires completed training, a valid licence for that truck type, supervised familiarisation on our aisles, racks and docks, and entry on the authorised-driver list.

4. Hand pallet jacks are limited to small, ground-level moves. They shall be used only by trained staff instructed in safe handling, load stability and pedestrian rules. They shall never be used to tow, to ride, to lift persons, or to move an unstable, overloaded or damaged pallet.

5. Rated capacities shall never be exceeded. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t, reach trucks at 2.0 t, and every capacity on site is built on a maximum pallet weight of 900 kg including the load. The driver shall check the load weight in the WMS task or on the label, respect the truck load plate and load centre, and refuse any lift that exceeds the rating or compromises stability.

6. Reach trucks are the only trucks permitted for high-bay work in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 pallet positions. Counterbalance forklifts shall not be used for high-level put-away or retrieval in the high bays except where the maintenance technician and shift supervisor have expressly confirmed suitability for the bay and height concerned.

7. Every truck shall receive a documented pre-use check before its first use each day. The driver assigned to first use on that day completes the check, records it on the daily check sheet or scanner log, and confirms the truck is fit for service. A truck without a completed daily check shall not be used.

8. The daily check covers the safety-critical items: brakes, steering, horn, lights and beacons, mirrors and cameras where fitted, seat belt and seat switch, forks, chains, hydraulics and leaks, tyres and wheels, battery charge and connections, emergency stop, and guards and markings. Any damage to racking, levellers or barriers found during the check shall also be reported.

9. Any defect affecting safe operation takes the truck out of service immediately. The driver shall park it clear of walkways, aisles and dock edges, tag it as do not use, inform the shift supervisor in charge of the floor, and enter the defect in the log for the maintenance technician. Only the maintenance technician shall return a quarantined truck to service and shall log every repair.

10. Trucks are shared across the two shifts, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, and Saturday overtime when approved. The outgoing driver shall report battery state, damage and faults at handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. The incoming driver shall verify the daily check status and re-check any truck reported faulty, changed, or left unattended in the yard.

11. Electric charging and battery handling shall follow the marked charging points only. Trucks shall not be parked, charged or left unattended in the 1.2 m wide pedestrian walkways, on crossings, in the 4.0 m main aisles, in the 3.0 m rack aisles, or on dock levellers and ramps. Keys shall be removed and the truck secured whenever the driver dismounts at the docks.

12. The shift supervisor enforces authorisation and check discipline on each shift under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Any unauthorised driving, missing daily check, exceeded capacity, or use of a tagged defective truck shall be stopped immediately and reported as an incident for follow-up by the warehouse manager.

title: Required PPE and seat belts
text:
1. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, with no exceptions. No task, rank, time pressure or short duration of entry justifies entering or working on the floor without them.

2. The warehouse floor means the entire 6,000 m2 single-storey hall, including Zones A to F, all transport aisles, rack aisles, pick faces, staging areas, dock areas at doors 1-8, and the packing, quarantine and hazmat areas in Zone F. The rule also applies in the fenced yard wherever people and trucks meet, at crossings, waiting areas and dock manoeuvres.

3. The rule applies to all persons on the floor: the warehouse manager, shift supervisors, forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, the maintenance technician, dispatchers, floaters, visitors, contractors and external drivers on the rare occasions they are authorised and accompanied beyond the marked waiting area.

4. High-visibility vests shall be worn closed and visible at all times on the floor, over all clothing including jackets and overalls. Torn, heavily soiled, faded or non-reflective vests shall not be used. Spare vests are kept at the hall entrances and issued by the shift supervisor in charge of the floor.

5. Safety footwear shall be class S3, correctly sized, fully laced or fastened, with intact toe protection, puncture-resistant sole and non-slip tread. Damaged, split, worn-smooth or makeshift footwear shall not be used. Open shoes, trainers and ordinary boots are prohibited on the floor.

6. Each person is responsible for wearing, checking and maintaining their own vest and footwear before starting work and after breaks. Any loss, damage or defect shall be reported to the shift supervisor immediately, and the person shall not start or continue floor work until replacement PPE is issued.

7. Forklift operators shall wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. This applies to all 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t and all 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t, in every zone, aisle, yard route and dock ramp, including short repositioning moves and manoeuvring at the 1.2 m high docks.

8. The seat belt shall be fastened before moving off, remain fastened for the whole movement, and be released only after the truck is fully stopped, secured and parked clear of walkways, aisles and dock edges. The belt shall sit correctly across the lap and hip, shall not be twisted, clamped, bypassed or extended with unauthorised devices, and the seat switch where fitted shall never be defeated.

9. Seat belts, anchorages and seat switches are part of the documented daily pre-use check before first use each day. Any fraying, faulty buckle, missing belt, defective retractor or faulty interlock takes the truck out of service immediately. The driver shall park, tag it as do not use, inform the shift supervisor, and only the maintenance technician shall return it to service and log the repair.

10. Riding as a passenger on a forklift, reach truck, electric pallet jack or hand pallet jack is prohibited. Carrying persons on forks, pallets or running boards is prohibited. Electric and hand pallet jacks without a fitted driver seat have no seat-belt requirement, but their operators remain subject to the hi-vis and S3 rules and to PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

11. Where additional protection is required for a specific task, for example in the Zone E cold zone, the Zone F ventilated hazmat cage, spill response, baler or stretch-wrapper work, it is worn in addition to, never instead of, the hi-vis vest and S3 footwear. External drivers and visitors who cannot be equipped shall remain in the marked waiting area and shall never enter the hall.

12. The shift supervisor enforces PPE and seat-belt discipline on each shift across the morning 06:00-14:00 and afternoon 14:00-22:00 shifts and any approved Saturday overtime. Any person without correct hi-vis or S3 footwear shall be removed from the floor immediately, any moving truck with an unbelted driver shall be stopped immediately, and every breach shall be reported as an incident for follow-up by the warehouse manager.

title: Racking and stacking limits
text:
1. No pallet on site, including the pallet itself, wrapping, and packaging, shall exceed 900 kg. This 900 kg full-weight pallet is the unit on which every rack, truck, and floor capacity is calculated, and it shall never be exceeded in storage, stacking, or transport.

2. All high-bay pallet racking in Zone B bulk storage, with 2,400 pallet positions, is rated bay by bay. Each rack bay shall carry at most 2,700 kg in total. The sum of all pallets stored in one bay, at all beam levels combined, shall remain within this limit at all times.

3. In practice the bay limit means at most three full-weight 900 kg pallets per bay. A fourth full-weight pallet shall never be added to a bay already holding three, and any combination of pallets whose combined weight would exceed 2,700 kg is prohibited, even if beam positions are physically free.

4. The weight of each pallet shall be known before put-away. Forklift and reach-truck drivers shall check the WMS task, goods label, or inbound documentation, and inbound operators and stock controllers shall flag any overweight, unstable, or damaged pallet in Zone A before it is booked and released to Zone B, E, or F.

5. Free block-stacking outside the racking is permitted only where marked and is limited to 3 pallets high and 3.5 m total height, including the pallet. Both limits apply together: stacking shall stop at whichever is reached first, and no fourth pallet shall be added even if the height remains below 3.5 m.

6. Block stacks shall be placed only on level, rated floor areas clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, the 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways with yellow barriers, crossings, dock levellers, ramps, and emergency exits. Staging in Zone D in front of doors 5-8 shall use wrapped, labelled pallets only and shall not obstruct dock manoeuvres.

7. Every stack shall be stable, uniformly built, and braced on an intact pallet. Damaged, cracked, wet, or leaning pallets, overhanging goods, and unwrapped unstable loads shall not be racked or block-stacked. They shall be reported to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found.

8. Only the 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t are permitted for high-bay put-away and retrieval in Zone B. Loads shall be lifted squarely, placed gently on beams without impact, and never pushed, dragged, or forced into the rack. Any strike, scrape, or deformation of uprights or beams shall be reported immediately and the bay unloaded if unsafe.

9. The Zone E cold zone between +2 °C and +6 °C and the Zone F ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 are subject to the same pallet and rack limits. Hazmat shall sit only in the cage and never more than 3,000 kg at a time, which is at most 3 full-weight pallets, and shall never be block-stacked outside the cage.

10. No person shall climb racking, walk on pallets, ride on forks, or use storage areas for access. Replenishment of pick faces in Zone C from bulk is done by truck only, and pickers shall pick from ground-level faces and flow racks only, never from high-bay beams.

11. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month, and any damage found during daily truck checks, put-away, picking, or cycle counts is reported to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and to the maintenance technician, who maintains racking and dock equipment and logs every repair. Damaged bays shall be offloaded and barriered until cleared.

12. The shift supervisor enforces racking and stacking limits on each shift under PR-02 Put-away to storage, PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, and PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Any overloaded bay, overweight pallet, over-high stack, or use of damaged racking or pallets shall be stopped immediately and reported as an incident for follow-up by the warehouse manager.

title: Supervision and shift handover
text:
1. The floor is never worked without supervision. On every shift — mornings 06:00-14:00, afternoons 14:00-22:00, and any approved Saturday morning overtime — one shift supervisor is in charge of the floor, the staff on it and the incident response.

2. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site — operations, safety and final sign-offs. The shift supervisor runs the shift on their behalf: enforcing speed limits, walkway segregation, PPE and seat-belt rules, racking and stacking limits, and stopping any unsafe work immediately.

3. Each shift is covered by its appointed supervisor, 2 dispatchers across the day, forklift operators, inbound operators or pickers according to the shift plan, and 2 floaters who cover absence. If the appointed supervisor is absent, a deputy is named before work starts — no shift starts without a named person in charge.

4. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime, including peak-season Saturday work. The supervisor shall not extend hours, add staff or restart work after an evacuation or incident without that approval and without confirming supervision, PPE and truck cover are in place.

5. Within their authority the shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR, approves the final disposition of inspected returns as restock, rework or scrap, and reviews every incident report from their shift. Write-offs above 750 EUR and the annual stocktake go to the warehouse manager for sign-off.

6. The supervisor assigns tasks only to authorised, equipped staff. Only licensed drivers on the authorised-driver list drive powered trucks, only trained staff use hand pallet jacks, and nobody works on the floor without high-visibility vest and class S3 footwear. Visitors and external drivers wait in the marked waiting area.

7. Every shift ends with a documented handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. The outgoing supervisor hands over directly to the incoming supervisor, face to face on the floor, and both sign the handover log. Where Saturday overtime follows, the same handover applies.

8. The safety part of the handover covers as a minimum: trucks in service and trucks tagged do not use, battery and charging state, daily check status, damage to racking, barriers, walkways and dock levellers, PPE shortages or defects, open incidents and near misses, and maintenance work logged for the technician.

9. The operational part covers: status at doors 1-4 inbound and doors 5-8 outbound against the dispatcher's door and slot plan, loads staged in Zone A and Zone D, pick-face replenishment outstanding in Zone C, Zone E cold-zone temperature and alarm status, quantity in the Zone F 60 m2 hazmat cage against the 3,000 kg limit, and quarantine and returns awaiting inspection.

10. The outgoing driver of each shared truck reports battery state, damage and faults at handover, and the incoming driver verifies the daily check status before first use. Any truck reported faulty, changed, or left unattended in the yard is re-checked before it moves.

11. Nothing unresolved is carried silently. Defects, overloaded bays, over-high stacks, blocked 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles or 1.2 m walkways, missing barrier sections, and cold-chain or hazmat alarms are entered in the log with the action taken and who owns the next step. The incoming supervisor checks that actions are closed or re-secured at the start of the shift.

12. The handover log is kept with the incident reports and daily truck checks for follow-up. The incoming supervisor briefs their shift on the handover points at shift start, and the warehouse manager reviews the logs, incident follow-up and overtime compliance as part of overall site accountability.

title: Cold zone rules
text:
1. Zone E is the only chilled storage area on site. It is a 300 m2 enclosed zone held continuously between +2 °C and +6 °C for packed chilled food, drugstore and household goods. No chilled goods shall be stored anywhere else.

2. The +2 °C to +6 °C range applies at all times, on both shifts, at night and at weekends. Doors, curtains, seals and insulation shall be kept closed and intact except for the immediate movement of goods or trucks. Doors left open or damaged seals shall be reported to the shift supervisor immediately.

3. Temperature is controlled automatically and monitored by fixed alarms. Any high, low or door-open alarm shall be treated as urgent. Staff shall alert the shift supervisor at once, protect the goods, close the zone, and work only under PR-12 Cold-chain handling until the temperature is back in range.

4. In addition to automatic monitoring, a manual temperature verification is carried out in Zone E on each shift. The appointed operator reads the display and a calibrated thermometer at the defined points, records the result with time and signature, and hands it to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor.

5. If a manual check or an alarm shows a deviation from +2 °C to +6 °C, the goods concerned shall not be picked, packed or dispatched until cleared. The stock controller and shift supervisor shall quarantine suspect stock, mark it clearly, and decide on inspection, release or scrap under damaged-goods and returns rules.

6. Only inspected and booked goods go to Zone E put-away, and pick faces fed from Zone E are replenished from bulk before the picking shift. Pallets in Zone E remain subject to the 900 kg maximum pallet weight, the 2,700 kg per rack bay limit and the block-stack limit of 3 pallets high and 3.5 m.

7. Work in Zone E follows normal traffic and pedestrian rules. The 8 km/h hall limit, 5 km/h at crossings and pedestrian zones, walkway discipline, and truck authorisation and daily checks apply in full. Condensation, wet floors and reduced visibility from cold air shall be treated as slip and driving hazards.
