8. Time in the cold zone shall be kept to the task. Staff shall prepare scanner tasks, labels and pallets before entry, work without delay inside, and close doors immediately after each entry and exit. No person shall remain in Zone E alone with closed doors without the shift supervisor knowing who is inside.

9. Warm protective clothing is worn in Zone E in addition to, never instead of, the mandatory high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear. Jackets, gloves and hats shall allow full movement, visibility of the vest, and safe operation of scanners, pallet jacks and reach trucks.

10. Forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks used in Zone E shall be suitable for cold and damp conditions. Drivers shall check brakes, steering, lights, horn and battery state with extra care, report loss of traction or misted lights and mirrors, and park and charge trucks only at the marked points outside the cold zone.

11. Hygiene and separation apply in Zone E. Damaged, leaking, open or unlabelled goods shall not be stored with intact chilled stock. They shall be moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, and any spill shall be cleaned and reported as an incident.

12. The shift supervisor enforces cold-zone discipline on each shift under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Any temperature deviation, missed manual verification, alarm failure, working without warm cover in addition to hi-vis and S3, or storage of chilled goods outside Zone E shall be stopped immediately and reported as an incident.

title: Hazmat storage rules
text:
1. Hazardous goods shall be stored only in the ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F. No hazmat shall sit anywhere else on site — not in Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone, or elsewhere in Zone F.

2. The cage is a separate, enclosed and ventilated unit of 60 m2 inside the 600 m2 Zone F services and control area. It is clearly marked, signed, lockable and kept closed except for immediate put-away, retrieval or inspection. Ventilation shall run continuously and shall never be blocked, switched off or used for storage.

3. The maximum stock in the cage at any one time is 3,000 kg in total. This is an absolute limit including all pallets, packaging and containers inside the cage combined, and it applies on both shifts, at night, at weekends and during overtime.

4. All site capacities are built on the maximum pallet weight of 900 kg including the load. The 3,000 kg cage limit therefore means at most 3 full-weight pallets in the cage. A fourth full-weight pallet shall never be added, even briefly, even if floor space is free.

5. Only inspected, correctly labelled and system-booked hazmat goes to the cage. Inbound operators check documents before unloading under PR-01, and only booked goods go to put-away under PR-02. Unchecked, unlabelled, damaged or leaking units shall not enter the cage and shall go to quarantine in Zone F the same day.

6. Pallets and racks in the cage remain subject to the standard limits: 900 kg per pallet maximum, 2,700 kg per rack bay maximum, and where block-stacking is marked, 3 pallets high and 3.5 m total height maximum. Hazmat shall never be block-stacked outside the cage or stacked above the marked height inside it.

7. The cage shall be kept orderly, dry and free of ignition sources, incompatible storage and unauthorised materials. Safety data sheets, spill kits and fire equipment for the stored classes shall be available at the cage entrance. Packing, repacking, decanting or rework of hazmat inside the cage is prohibited — value-added work belongs in the packing area under PR-13 only.

8. Access to the cage is restricted to instructed staff on defined tasks. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor controls who enters, and the quantity inside is tracked pallet by pallet in the WMS. The handover on every shift verifies the quantity in the 60 m2 cage against the 3,000 kg limit.

9. Traffic and handling rules apply in full at the cage. The 8 km/h hall limit, 5 km/h at crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps, walkway discipline, and driver authorisation with documented daily truck checks apply. Only authorised forklift operators drive powered trucks to and into the cage, and trucks shall never be parked or charged inside it.

10. Mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear apply in and around the cage with no exceptions. Any additional protection required for the stored classes under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response is worn in addition to, never instead of, hi-vis and S3. Staff without correct PPE shall not enter.

11. Any damage, leak, open container, missing label, failed ventilation, or stock approaching the 3,000 kg limit shall be reported to the shift supervisor immediately. Suspect goods shall be moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, and any spill shall be contained, cleaned and reported as an incident under PR-13.

12. The shift supervisor enforces hazmat storage discipline on each shift under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response and PR-02 Put-away to storage. Any hazmat outside the cage, any stock above 3,000 kg, or any use of the cage for non-hazmat storage shall be stopped immediately and reported as an incident for follow-up by the warehouse manager.

title: Spills, quarantine and damage
text:
1. Any spill, leak or damaged container shall be treated as a safety event first and a stock event second. Work around the spill stops immediately, the area is secured against trucks and pedestrians, and the shift supervisor in charge of the floor is alerted at once under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.

2. The person finding the spill shall not touch, move, wipe or dilute unknown substances without instruction. Ventilation in the Zone F hazmat cage is left running, ignition sources are kept away, and additional protection required under PR-13 is worn in addition to, never instead of, the mandatory high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear.

3. Small contained spills are contained at source with the spill kit held at the hazmat cage entrance and at the defined points in Zone F. Absorbent material, barriers and personal protection from the kit shall be used as instructed, and contaminated absorbents are bagged, labelled and held in quarantine for disposal — never put back in racking, in general waste or in drains.

4. Large, spreading, vapour-forming or unidentified spills are not cleaned by floor staff. The zone is evacuated and closed, the supervisor calls the defined response, and re-entry is only on supervisor instruction after ventilation, clearance and documented clean-up. Any spill in Zone E between +2 °C and +6 °C is also treated as a hygiene event and suspect chilled stock is quarantined.

5. Every spill, including a fully cleaned minor drip, is reported as an incident on the shift. The report records what spilled, where, quantity, cause, who was exposed, what kit was used and how waste was secured. The shift supervisor reviews every report and the maintenance technician restores and logs any kit, racking or floor repair.

6. Damaged, leaking, open, unlabelled or otherwise suspect goods shall not stay on a pick face, in a rack bay, on a dock or in a truck. They are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, by a safe route at 8 km/h in the hall and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and on dock ramps.

7. Quarantine is a separate, clearly marked and segregated area in the 600 m2 Zone F services and control area, apart from the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, packing, returns inspection and sound stock. Only quarantined goods sit there, clearly labelled with date, origin zone, reason and finder, and physically held so they cannot be picked, replenished to Zone C, staged in Zone D or dispatched.

8. Returns come back through Zone F and pass the same control. They are accepted within 14 days of delivery, every unit is inspected by returns staff, and only then is a disposition proposed as restock, rework or scrap under PR-07 Returns handling. Damaged returns go to quarantine the same day and are never restocked without inspection and approval.

9. No quarantined goods leave quarantine without a documented decision. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns as restock, rework or scrap, and approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Unsafe, contaminated or unidentifiable goods are directed to scrap or authorised disposal.

10. Any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR goes to the warehouse manager for sign-off. The manager also signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results. No adjustment or write-off is posted without a second count by the stock controllers under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

11. Restock from quarantine is released only after inspection confirms intact, labelled, in-date and system-correct goods. Only inspected and booked goods go to put-away in Zone B, E or F under PR-02, and all pallet and bay limits continue to apply: 900 kg per pallet maximum, 2,700 kg per rack bay, block-stacking 3 pallets high and 3.5 m, and never more than 3,000 kg in the hazmat cage.

12. The shift supervisor enforces spill, quarantine and damage discipline on each shift under PR-09, PR-07 and PR-13 and verifies quarantine and cage status at handover under PR-15. Any unreported spill, missing spill kit, goods left outside quarantine, or release or write-off without the required approval shall be stopped immediately and reported as an incident for follow-up by the warehouse manager.

title: Reporting incidents
text:
1. Every unsafe event is reported. This means any injury, near miss, collision or fall, speeding or failure to give way, pedestrian in a truck area, breach of hi-vis, S3 footwear or seat-belt rules, damage to racking, pallets, barriers, walkways, dock levellers or trucks, any spill or leak, any temperature or hazmat alarm, and any overloaded bay, overweight pallet or over-high stack.

2. The first duty is to make safe and alert. The person involved or finding the event stops work, secures the area against trucks and pedestrians, gives first aid or raises the alarm if anyone is hurt, and informs the shift supervisor in charge of the floor at once, on the morning 06:00-14:00 shift, the afternoon 14:00-22:00 shift and any approved Saturday overtime.

3. No incident scene is cleared before the supervisor sees it, except to protect people, prevent fire or spill spread, or keep the +2 °C to +6 °C cold chain closed. Trucks involved stay parked with keys removed, goods stay where they are, and quarantine moves under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling happen only on supervisor instruction.

4. The report is made on the shift on which the event happened. The person involved, the finder and any witness each give their account to the supervisor before end of shift. The outgoing supervisor includes open incidents and near misses in the documented handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover so nothing is carried silently.

5. Each incident report records as a minimum: date, time and zone, who was involved and who reported, what happened and what truck, rack, door or goods were concerned, injury or damage caused, immediate action taken, and whether the maintenance technician, stock controller or dispatcher was called. Spill reports also record substance, quantity, kit used and waste secured under PR-13.

6. Damage is reported the same way as injury and near miss. Any strike to a rack upright or beam in Zone B bulk storage, barrier, yellow walkway protection, dock leveller at doors 1-8, truck, pallet or building is reported immediately to the supervisor, even if no injury occurred and the damage looks minor.

7. Damaged racking, barriers, walkways and dock equipment are taken out of use until cleared. The supervisor barriers the bay, aisle section, walkway part or leveller, stops put-away, replenishment and dock work there, and calls the maintenance technician, who maintains trucks, racking and dock equipment and logs every repair.

8. Damaged, leaking, open or unlabelled goods are moved to quarantine in the 600 m2 Zone F services area the same day they are found, on supervisor instruction and by a safe route. They are labelled with date, origin zone, reason and finder and are held so they cannot be picked in Zone C, staged in Zone D or dispatched.

9. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report from their shift. They check the facts, confirm the area is secured, order containment, quarantine, recount or repair, decide restock, rework or scrap for inspected returns and write-offs up to 750 EUR, and send the reviewed report for follow-up.

10. The warehouse manager follows up all reviewed reports as part of overall site accountability. The manager reviews logs, truck checks and handover records, approves damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR, signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake, and authorises any change to procedures PR-01 to PR-15 arising from the event.

11. No adjustment or write-off is posted without a second count. Stock controllers recount under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts before any inventory correction, and the dispatcher holds any outbound load from doors 5-8 if the goods, pallets or documents are affected until the supervisor releases it.

12. Reports, handover logs, daily truck checks and repair logs are kept together for review. The incoming supervisor briefs the next shift on lessons and re-secured areas at shift start, and repeated speeding, unauthorised driving, PPE breaches or rack damage are treated as disciplinary matters under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

title: Evacuation and assembly point
text:
1. When the evacuation alarm sounds or the order to evacuate is given, all work stops immediately. Staff shut down safe equipment where it can be done in seconds, leave goods, scanners and paperwork where they are, and move at once to the nearest marked emergency exit under PR-14 Emergency evacuation.

2. Trucks are stopped and secured without delay. Drivers brake, lower forks, switch off the truck, remove the key, and leave it clear of the 1.2 m walkways, crossings, dock levellers and emergency exits. No truck moves during an evacuation, and dock loading and unloading at doors 1-8 stops.

3. Everyone leaves by the marked pedestrian routes. Staff in Zones A to F use the 1.2 m wide walkways with yellow barriers and the signposted exits, not the 4.0 m transport aisles or dock manoeuvring areas unless the marked route requires a crossing. Running, overtaking and re-entering for belongings are prohibited.

4. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor directs the evacuation on the shift. The outgoing order is simple: leave the 6,000 m2 single-storey hall and the office annex, keep walkways and yard routes passable for emergency vehicles, and go directly to the assembly point by the north fence.

5. Staff from the Zone E cold zone leave through the nearest exit, close the cold-room doors behind them if it can be done instantly, and do not stop to move stock. Staff in the Zone F hazmat cage and packing area leave ventilation running, leave spill kits and goods in place, and close the cage and quarantine doors if instant.

6. Visitors, contractors and external drivers are included in the evacuation. Inbound operators, dispatchers and supervisors escort anyone authorised beyond the marked waiting area to the assembly point. No driver or visitor remains in the waiting area, at a dock door or in a trailer.

7. The assembly point is at the marked area by the north fence in the fenced yard, clear of docks, trailer movements and emergency access. All evacuees gather there by team, keep together, and remain there until formally released. No one leaves the assembly point or the site without reporting to the supervisor.

8. Roll call starts immediately at the assembly point and is completed before anyone re-enters the building. The shift supervisor takes the roll against the shift attendance, handover log and visitor and driver register, supported by dispatchers. Missing persons are reported at once and no search is made by floor staff.

9. The supervisor accounts for both shifts at changeover and for any approved Saturday morning overtime: outgoing staff, incoming staff, floaters covering absence, maintenance work and any carriers signed in for doors 1-4 inbound and doors 5-8 outbound. Absence from roll call is treated as missing until confirmed.

10. No one re-enters the hall, office annex or yard work areas until the shift supervisor gives the all-clear after the cause is cleared and the building is declared safe. The supervisor confirms with the warehouse manager and, where called, the emergency services that heat, smoke, spill, structural or racking danger is removed.

11. After the all-clear the supervisor directs controlled re-entry by team through the normal entrances, checks Zones A to F, docks, levellers, racking and barriers for damage, and holds any affected bay, aisle, walkway or door out of use until the maintenance technician inspects and logs the repair. Cold-chain and hazmat alarms are re-checked before restart.

12. Every evacuation, including drills, is recorded and followed up. The supervisor logs time, cause, roll-call result and defects, reviews it as an incident report, and briefs the next shift at handover under PR-15. An evacuation drill with full roll call at the north fence is run every quarter, and failures to assemble, missing registers or blocked exits are corrected immediately.

title: Inspections, drills and follow-up
text:
1. Scheduled checks keep the site safe between incidents. They run to a fixed calendar whether the operation is busy or not, on mornings 06:00-14:00, afternoons 14:00-22:00 and any approved Saturday overtime, and no time pressure justifies skipping, shortening or signing off an unchecked item.

2. Every powered truck gets a documented pre-use check before its first use each day. This covers the 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, the 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t, the 11 electric pallet jacks and any hand pallet jack in transport use, and includes brakes, steering, horn, lights and beacons, mirrors, seat belt and seat switch, forks, chains, hydraulics, tyres, battery and emergency stop.

3. The driver assigned to first use completes and records the daily check on the sheet or scanner log. A truck without a completed check shall not be used. Any defect affecting safety takes the truck out of service immediately, parked clear, tagged do not use, reported to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor, and only the maintenance technician returns it to service and logs every repair.

4. Racking in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 pallet positions receives a documented safety inspection every month. The inspection checks uprights, beams, fixings, bay load notices against the 2,700 kg per bay limit, pallet condition against the 900 kg maximum, and block-stack areas against 3 pallets high and 3.5 m.

5. Any rack damage found during the monthly inspection, or during daily truck checks, put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03, picking or cycle counts, is barriered and offloaded at once. The bay stays out of use until the maintenance technician inspects, repairs and logs clearance, and the event is reported as an incident.

6. Zone E cold-zone checks run every shift. In addition to continuous automatic control between +2 °C and +6 °C with alarms, a manual temperature verification is carried out on each shift at the defined points with a calibrated thermometer, recorded with time and signature and handed to the shift supervisor.

7. Any deviation, alarm, door-seal failure or missed verification in the 300 m2 Zone E is treated as urgent under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Suspect stock is quarantined in Zone F the same day, not picked, packed or dispatched, and restart is only after temperature is back in range and the supervisor releases the goods.

8. Walkways, barriers, markings and dock equipment are checked every shift. The supervisor confirms the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, crossings, 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles, dock levellers at doors 1-8 and the 60 m2 hazmat cage ventilation are clear, intact and passable, and the maintenance technician restores faded markings and logs repairs.

9. Inventory discipline supports safety follow-up. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule and once a year the site shuts for a full wall-to-wall stocktake signed off by the warehouse manager. No adjustment is posted without a second count under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

10. An evacuation drill with full roll call at the assembly point by the north fence is run every quarter under PR-14 Emergency evacuation. Roll call is completed before anyone re-enters the 6,000 m2 hall, and time, attendance, missing registers, blocked exits and defects are logged and reviewed as an incident.

11. Every check, inspection and drill ends in documented follow-up. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report from their shift, orders containment, quarantine, recount or repair, decides returns disposition and write-offs up to 750 EUR, and hands open points to the next shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

12. The warehouse manager owns overall follow-up as accountable for operations and safety. The manager reviews logs, truck checks, handover records and drill results, approves damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR, signs off the annual stocktake, authorises changes to PR-01 to PR-15, and treats repeated missed checks, unauthorised driving or uncorrected defects as disciplinary matters.

title: Warehouse Manager
text:
1. The Warehouse Manager is accountable for the whole Harborwick 3PL site in Port Sellow — all operations, safety, inventory accuracy and legal compliance across the 6,000 m2 hall, the office annex and the 3,500 m2 fenced yard. What is in the system must be what is on the rack.

2. The Manager leads a team of about 38-40 people: 2 shift supervisors, 8 forklift operators, 6 inbound operators, 10 pickers, 2 stock controllers, 4 returns and packing staff, 1 maintenance technician, 2 dispatchers and 2 floaters. The Manager sets organisation of the two shifts, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, and ensures one shift supervisor is always in charge of the floor.

3. The Manager owns the fifteen written procedures PR-01 to PR-15 and ensures they are applied as described in the warehouse brief. Where a manual and the brief conflict, the brief prevails. In particular the Manager enforces the end-to-end goods flow: document check before unloading in Zone A, inspection before system booking, booking before put-away to Zone B, E or F, replenishment of Zone C before each picking shift, scan-verified picking, wrapping and labelling in Zone D, and dispatcher release before loading and sealing.

4. The Manager is responsible for capacity and layout discipline across Zones A-F. This includes the division of inbound Doors 1-4 and outbound Doors 5-8, the 2,400 pallet positions in Zone B bulk storage with a 2,700 kg limit per rack bay, the 3-pallet and 3.5 m limit for block stacking, the 900 kg maximum per pallet including load, the 28 full-weight pallets per 26,000 kg trailer and the 448 full-weight pallets per shift outbound maximum through the four outbound doors, and the limits in Zone E and Zone F, including a maximum of 3,000 kg and 3 full-weight pallets in the 60 m2 hazmat cage.

5. The Manager is accountable for safety on site. This includes the 8 km/h limit inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles, the 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways, mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the warehouse floor, seat belts for forklift operators when moving, daily documented checks before first use of each truck, monthly documented racking inspections, and quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point before re-entry.

6. The Manager is accountable for inventory integrity and cold-chain and hazmat control. This includes daily cycle counts on a rotating schedule, the annual wall-to-wall stocktake, the rule that no adjustment is posted without a second count, same-day quarantine of damaged goods, inspection of all returns in Zone F within 14 days of delivery, chilled storage in Zone E at +2 °C to +6 °C with alarms and manual verification each shift, and storage of hazmat only in the ventilated cage.

7. The following sign-offs and approvals are exclusive to the Warehouse Manager and may not be delegated:

a) sign-off of the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results;

b) approval of any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR — the shift supervisor may approve only up to 750 EUR;

c) approval of all overtime;

d) authorisation of new forklift operators — no licence, no truck, and no operation of the 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts, 2.0 t reach trucks, electric or hand pallet jacks without this authorisation.

8. The Manager ensures that delegated authorities are respected: the shift supervisor runs the shift, responds to incidents and reviews every incident report, approves write-offs up to 750 EUR and the final disposition of inspected returns; the dispatcher owns dock scheduling, door and time-slot assignment and release of outbound loads.

title: Shift Supervisors
text:
1. The Shift Supervisor is in charge of the warehouse floor for their assigned shift — mornings 06:00-14:00 or afternoons 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when authorised. There are two Shift Supervisors in total and one is always present and accountable while the shift is running.

2. Each Shift Supervisor directs the floor staff on shift: inbound operators, forklift operators, pickers, returns and packing staff, stock controllers, the maintenance technician and floaters as allocated. The Supervisor assigns tasks, balances workload across Zones A to F, ensures replenishment of Zone C pick faces before picking starts, and ensures handover to the next shift is completed under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. The Supervisor enforces the end-to-end goods flow on shift. No truck is unloaded in Zone A at Doors 1-4 until documents are checked, no goods are booked until counted and inspected under PR-01, and no goods move to put-away in Zone B, Zone E or Zone F until booked under PR-02. In Zone D only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged at outbound Doors 5-8, and no load is moved for loading and sealing until released by the dispatcher under PR-06.

4. The Supervisor is responsible for safety, order and discipline on shift under PR-10 and PR-11. This includes the 8 km/h limit inside the 6,000 m2 hall, 12 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard, and 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, use of the 1.2 m physically separated walkways, keeping 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles clear, and keeping drivers in the marked waiting area and out of the hall.

5. The Supervisor enforces personal protective equipment and equipment rules on every shift. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor without exception, and seat belts are mandatory for forklift operators whenever the truck is moving. No person operates the 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts, 2.0 t reach trucks, electric pallet jacks or hand pallet jacks without authorisation by the Warehouse Manager, and no truck is used for first use on the day without its documented check.

6. The Supervisor leads first response to any incident, near-miss, damage, spill, cold-chain alarm or evacuation on shift. The Supervisor secures the area, protects people and goods, calls the Warehouse Manager and emergency services as required, ensures damaged goods go to quarantine the same day under PR-09, and ensures every incident report is completed and then reviewed by the Supervisor before further action.

7. Within delegated authority, the Shift Supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 750 EUR and approves the final disposition of inspected returns — restock, rework or scrap — after inspection in Zone F under PR-07. Write-offs above 750 EUR, sign-off of the annual wall-to-wall stocktake, approval of overtime, and authorisation of new forklift operators are reserved exclusively to the Warehouse Manager and are escalated without exception.

8. The Supervisor supports inventory accuracy, cold-chain and hazmat discipline on shift. This includes cooperation with daily cycle counts on the rotating zone schedule with no adjustment without a second count under PR-08, manual temperature verification each shift in the +2 °C to +6 °C Zone E under PR-12, keeping hazmat only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage up to 3,000 kg under PR-13, respecting the 900 kg maximum per pallet and the rack-bay and stacking limits, and leading quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point before anyone re-enters under PR-14.

title: Dispatchers
text:
1. The Dispatchers — two in total — own transport booking, dock-door scheduling and outbound load release for Harborwick 3PL Ltd. They are the single point of contact for carriers and for clients on delivery and collection timing, and no truck arrives, unloads, loads or departs without their booking and instruction.

2. Each Dispatcher books inbound and outbound transport against operational capacity and client promise. The booking respects the site limits: inbound Doors 1-4 only and outbound Doors 5-8 only in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard at 1.2 m dock height, a maximum of 900 kg per pallet including load, 28 full-weight pallets per contracted 26,000 kg curtain-side trailer on 33 floor positions, two full-weight pallets per 1,800 kg delivery van on 6 positions with anything heavier by trailer, and a maximum of 448 full-weight pallets per shift through the four outbound doors at 4 trailer loads per door per shift.

3. The Dispatcher assigns every carrier a specific dock door and a time slot before arrival and communicates it in advance. Inbound carriers are assigned only to Doors 1-4 in Zone A and outbound carriers only to Doors 5-8 in Zone D. The Dispatcher sequences arrivals to avoid yard congestion, keeps the marked driver waiting area in use, and enforces the rule that drivers wait in the waiting area and never enter the 6,000 m2 hall.

4. On the day of operation the Dispatcher controls the dock plan in real time. This includes confirming truck arrival against its slot, authorising movement to the assigned door and leveller, coordinating with the Shift Supervisor on labour and equipment readiness in Zone A receiving and Zone D dispatch, and re-assigning doors and slots when trucks are early, late or cancelled. Any change to door assignment is issued by the Dispatcher and no floor staff changes it independently.

5. The Dispatcher enforces outbound discipline under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. No load is loaded or sealed until the Dispatcher has released it. Release is given only when picking in Zone C is scan-verified, goods are packed and labelled under PR-05, pallets in Zone D are wrapped on the semi-automatic stretch wrappers and labelled and staged for the correct outbound door, and system quantities match the staged load. The Dispatcher stops any release where documentation, quantities or labelling do not match.

6. For inbound, the Dispatcher supports the Zone A flow under PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-02 Put-away to storage. Documents are checked before unloading, goods are unloaded, counted and inspected before system booking, and only booked goods go to put-away in Zone B, E or F. The Dispatcher does not authorise put-away, but withholds the next inbound call to a door until the Shift Supervisor confirms Zone A is clear for the next truck.

7. The Dispatcher maintains the transport and dispatch records: carrier bookings, door and time-slot allocations, arrival and departure times, trailer and seal numbers, load releases, and any delay, damage or refusal at loading. Records feed the end-of-shift handover under PR-15, incident reporting to the Shift Supervisor, and same-day quarantine of any damaged goods found at dispatch under PR-09.

8. The Dispatcher works to site safety and authority rules. This includes the 12 km/h yard limit and 5 km/h limit in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, the 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways, mandatory high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear on the warehouse floor, and the hazmat limit of 3,000 kg and 3 full-weight pallets in the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F. The Dispatcher does not approve overtime, write-offs, return dispositions or forklift authorisations — overtime and write-offs above 750 EUR are escalated to the Warehouse Manager, write-offs up to 750 EUR, incident review and floor incident response to the Shift Supervisor.

title: Inbound Operators
text:
1. The Inbound Operators — six in total — are responsible for unloading, counting, inspection and handover to booked stock in Zone A receiving. They work the 800 m2 receiving area in front of inbound Doors 1-4 and no goods move past Zone A to Zone B, E or F until their checks are complete under PR-01 Inbound receiving.

2. Inbound Operators work under the direction of the Shift Supervisor on shift — mornings 06:00-14:00 or afternoons 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager. They coordinate with forklift operators, stock controllers and the Dispatcher on door readiness and complete handover to the next shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. No truck is touched until the paperwork is checked. The Inbound Operator verifies the carrier is at the Dispatcher-assigned door and time slot, checks delivery documents against the booking, and only then starts unloading. Any mismatch in supplier, quantity, door or documentation is stopped and reported to the Shift Supervisor before unloading continues.

4. Unloading, counting and inspection are completed for every delivery. The Operator unloads pallets and cartons safely at the 1.2 m dock with the door leveller, counts all units by piece and pallet, inspects packaging, labelling, expiry and visible damage, and records shortages, overages and damage. Only counted and inspected goods are presented for system booking, and only booked goods go to put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage.

5. The Operator prepares the handover to booked stock. Inspected pallets are segregated by client and destination — Zone B bulk storage, Zone E cold zone or Zone F services and control — with the 900 kg maximum per pallet including load respected, labels and counts confirmed, and the location cleared for forklift collection. Zone A is kept clear between trucks so the Dispatcher can call the next vehicle only when the Supervisor confirms readiness.

6. Inbound Operators apply cold-chain and special-goods rules at receipt. Chilled goods for the 300 m2 Zone E are prioritised for immediate transfer to the +2 °C to +6 °C store with alarms, hazmat is identified and sent only to the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F within the 3,000 kg and 3 full-weight pallet limit, and any damaged goods found are moved to quarantine the same day under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

7. Safety and pedestrian discipline are enforced in Zone A under PR-10 and PR-11. The Operators observe the 8 km/h limit inside the 6,000 m2 hall, 12 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard and 5 km/h at crossings, dock ramps and the 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways, keep the 4.0 m main transport aisles clear, and ensure drivers remain in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor without exception.

8. Inbound Operators do not operate the 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts or 2.0 t reach trucks unless individually authorised by the Warehouse Manager, and no truck is used for first use on the day without its documented check. They use hand and electric pallet jacks only if authorised, report every incident, spill, near-miss or rack damage to the Shift Supervisor for review, and support daily cycle counts with no adjustment without a second count under PR-08 and quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point under PR-14.

title: Forklift Operators
text:
1. The Forklift Operators — eight in total — are the only staff authorised to operate powered materials-handling equipment on a regular basis. They drive the all-electric fleet across all Zones A to F: 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t for general work and 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t for the high bays in Zone B, plus 11 electric pallet jacks for staging and replenishment moves.

2. No licence, no truck. No person operates a counterbalance forklift, reach truck, electric or hand pallet jack as a Forklift Operator without individual authorisation by the Warehouse Manager. Operators work under the Shift Supervisor on shift — mornings 06:00-14:00 or afternoons 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved — and complete handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. Every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. The Operator completes the checklist for the truck assigned to them, reports any defect, fluid leak, alarm, brake, steering, fork, chain, light or horn fault, and does not use the truck until the Shift Supervisor and the maintenance technician clear it. The check is recorded and every repair is logged.

4. Forklift Operators perform all pallet transport between zones: collection of booked pallets from Zone A receiving for put-away to Zone B, E or F under PR-02, replenishment of Zone C pick faces from bulk before each picking shift under PR-03, movement of wrapped and labelled pallets to Zone D dispatch staging under PR-05 and PR-06, and transfers to quarantine and to the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F under PR-09 and PR-13.

5. Load limits are respected on every move. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 900 kg. Each rack bay in the 2,400-position high-bay store in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg, free block-stacking elsewhere is limited to 3 pallets high and 3.5 m, and the hazmat cage holds never more than 3,000 kg, or 3 full-weight pallets, at a time. Overweight, unstable or damaged pallets are stopped and reported to the Shift Supervisor.

6. Speed and right-of-way rules are enforced without exception. The limits are 8 km/h inside the 6,000 m2 hall, 12 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet — marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Operators use only the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles, give way to pedestrians at all times, and never enter the 1.2 m physically separated walkways protected by yellow barriers.

7. Dock and pedestrian discipline applies on every task under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Operators serve only the Dispatcher-assigned door — inbound Doors 1-4 in Zone A and outbound Doors 5-8 in Zone D at 1.2 m dock height — using the door leveller provided, keep drivers in the marked waiting area and out of the hall, and stop work on any spill, cold-chain alarm or incident until the Shift Supervisor secures the area.

8. Safety equipment and reporting are mandatory. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are required for everyone on the warehouse floor with no exceptions, and seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving. Operators support daily cycle counts under PR-08 with no adjustment without a second count, manual temperature discipline in the +2 °C to +6 °C Zone E under PR-12, quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point under PR-14, and report every incident, near-miss or rack damage to the Shift Supervisor for review.

title: Pickers
text:
1. The Pickers — ten in total — are responsible for scanner-directed picking of customer orders in Zone C picking. They work the 1,200 m2 area of ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from bulk storage, and no picked goods move to Zone D dispatch until picking and verification are complete under PR-04 Order picking.

2. Pickers work under the direction of the Shift Supervisor on shift — mornings 06:00-14:00 or afternoons 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager. They start only after the pick faces in Zone C have been replenished from bulk storage under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, and complete handover to the next shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. All picking is driven by scanner tasks. The Picker logs on with one of the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners, follows the task sequence location by location, picks only the instructed quantity from the instructed pick face, and confirms each pick in the system. No picking from bulk storage in Zone B, from Zone E, or from the hazmat cage and quarantine in Zone F is done on picker initiative — any face running empty or damaged is reported to the Shift Supervisor for replenishment.

4. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed under PR-04 and PR-05. The Picker scans each item and its location label, checks product, quantity, batch and expiry against the task, and only then places it in the order carton, tote or pallet. Any scan mismatch, shortage, damage or expiry issue is stopped, segregated and reported to the Shift Supervisor, and the quantity is never force-confirmed in the system.

5. The Picker prepares the transfer to dispatch. Verified picks are packed, labelled with the correct customer and order label under PR-05 Packing and labelling, and moved to the Zone D staging area in front of outbound Doors 5-8. Only correctly labelled units are presented for wrapping on the semi-automatic stretch wrappers, only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged for their outbound door, and no load is loaded or sealed until released by the Dispatcher under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

6. Pickers apply weight, cold-chain and special-goods rules in Zone C. The 900 kg maximum per pallet including load is respected on every pallet built, chilled lines for the 300 m2 Zone E are picked promptly and returned to the +2 °C to +6 °C store without delay under PR-12 Cold-chain handling, and any damaged goods found are moved to quarantine the same day under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Returns within 14 days of delivery and hazmat handling are not picker tasks.

7. Safety and pedestrian discipline are observed at the pick face under PR-10 and PR-11. Pickers keep the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles clear, use only the 1.2 m physically separated pedestrian walkways protected by yellow barriers, and give way to forklifts and reach trucks at all times. The limits of 8 km/h inside the 6,000 m2 hall, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are respected, and drivers remain in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall.

8. Pickers wear high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the warehouse floor without exception. They do not operate the 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts or 2.0 t reach trucks unless individually authorised by the Warehouse Manager, and use electric or hand pallet jacks only if authorised and only after the documented daily check for first use. They report every incident, near-miss, spill or rack damage to the Shift Supervisor for review, support daily cycle counts with no adjustment without a second count under PR-08, and take part in quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point under PR-14.

title: Returns and Packing Staff
text:
1. The Returns and Packing Staff — four in total — are responsible for returns inspection in Zone F and for value-added packing and labelling. They work the 600 m2 Zone F services and control area covering packing stations, quarantine and returns inspection, including the separate 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, and no return is restocked, reworked or scrapped without their inspection under PR-07 Returns handling.

2. Returns and Packing Staff work under the direction of the Shift Supervisor on shift — mornings 06:00-14:00 or afternoons 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager. They coordinate with inbound operators, pickers, forklift operators, stock controllers and the Dispatcher on priorities and complete handover to the next shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. Returns are accepted only within 14 days of delivery through Zone F. The staff member verifies the return against delivery documents and the booking, checks that the carrier used the assigned door and that drivers remain in the marked waiting area, and refuses undocumented or out-of-time returns to the Shift Supervisor before any unloading to inspection.

4. Every returned unit is inspected. Under PR-07 the staff check product identity, quantity, batch, expiry, packaging, labelling, temperature history for chilled lines, and visible damage or contamination, record the result unit by unit, and segregate goods by proposed route. Inspection only — the final disposition of restock, rework or scrap is approved by the Shift Supervisor, write-offs up to 750 EUR by the Supervisor and above 750 EUR exclusively by the Warehouse Manager.

5. Inspected returns are proposed for restock, rework or scrap. Clean, saleable and in-date units in intact packaging are proposed for restock and presented for system booking before any put-away to Zone B, E or F under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Units needing relabelling, repacking or cleaning are proposed for rework in Zone F. Unsaleable, expired, contaminated or irreparably damaged units are proposed for scrap and moved to quarantine the same day they are found under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. No adjustment is posted without a second count under PR-08.

6. The staff perform packing and labelling under PR-05 Packing and labelling. Scan-verified picks from Zone C and reworked units from Zone F are packed to order, labelled with the correct client, product, quantity and destination labels, and handed to forklift movement to Zone D. Only correctly labelled units go forward; in Zone D only wrapped and labelled pallets on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers are staged at outbound Doors 5-8, and no load is loaded or sealed until released by the Dispatcher under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

7. Cold-chain and hazmat rules are applied in Zone F under PR-12 and PR-13. Chilled returns for the 300 m2 Zone E are prioritised for immediate return to the +2 °C to +6 °C store with alarms and manual verification each shift. Hazmat sits only in the ventilated cage, never elsewhere and never more than 3,000 kg or 3 full-weight pallets at a time. The 900 kg maximum per pallet including load, the 2,700 kg limit per rack bay, and the 3-pallet and 3.5 m block-stacking limit are respected on every pallet built.

8. Safety, equipment and reporting discipline apply without exception. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor, the 8 km/h limit inside the 6,000 m2 hall, 12 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed, and the 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m physically separated walkways are kept clear under PR-10 and PR-11. Staff do not operate the 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts or 2.0 t reach trucks unless individually authorised by the Warehouse Manager and use pallet jacks only if authorised after the documented daily check. Every incident, spill, near-miss or rack damage is reported to the Shift Supervisor for review, daily cycle counts are supported, and quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point are attended under PR-14.

title: Stock Controllers
text:
1. The Stock Controllers — two in total — own inventory accuracy day to day for Harborwick 3PL Ltd. They are accountable for ensuring that the stock in the system is the stock on the rack across Zones A to F, including the 2,400 pallet positions in Zone B bulk storage, the 300 m2 Zone E cold zone and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F.

2. Stock Controllers work under the direction of the Shift Supervisor on shift — mornings 06:00-14:00 or afternoons 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager. They coordinate with inbound operators, forklift operators, pickers, returns and packing staff and the Dispatcher, and complete handover to the next shift under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. The Stock Controllers plan the daily count by zone and location, execute counts using the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners, and ensure all zones are covered on rotation without disrupting receiving in Zone A, replenishment of Zone C pick faces, or staging in Zone D in front of outbound Doors 5-8.

4. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Where the first count differs from the system, the Stock Controller orders an independent recount, investigates document checks, bookings, put-away under PR-02, picking under PR-04 and dispatch under PR-06, and only then posts the adjustment in the system. All counts, recounts and adjustments are recorded with location, product, batch, quantity, counter and reason.

5. Once a year the site shuts down for a full wall-to-wall stocktake. The Stock Controllers prepare locations, labels and scanner readiness, lead the counting teams on the floor, reconcile every difference with recounts, and present the results for sign-off. Sign-off of the annual stocktake results is exclusive to the Warehouse Manager and is never delegated.

6. Stock Controllers control damaged-goods and quarantine accuracy under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Any damaged goods found during counts are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, segregated in the system, and reported to the Shift Supervisor. Write-offs up to and including 750 EUR are approved by the Shift Supervisor, write-offs above 750 EUR exclusively by the Warehouse Manager, and no scrapped unit leaves the books without that approval.

7. The Controllers apply quantity and storage discipline on every count. The 900 kg maximum per pallet including load, the 2,700 kg limit per rack bay, the 3-pallet and 3.5 m block-stacking limit, and the 3,000 kg and 3 full-weight pallet limit in the hazmat cage are verified. Chilled lines for Zone E at +2 °C to +6 °C with alarms and manual verification each shift and returns within 14 days of delivery through Zone F are checked for system-location match, and mismatches are corrected only after recount.

8. Safety, equipment and reporting rules apply without exception. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor, the 8 km/h limit inside the 6,000 m2 hall, 12 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed, and the 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m physically separated walkways are kept clear under PR-10 and PR-11. Stock Controllers do not operate the 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts or 2.0 t reach trucks unless individually authorised by the Warehouse Manager, use pallet jacks only if authorised, report every incident, spill, near-miss or rack damage to the Shift Supervisor for review, and take part in quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point under PR-14.

title: Maintenance Technician
text:
1. The Maintenance Technician — one in total — is responsible for the upkeep of all materials-handling equipment, racking and dock equipment at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. All repairs are logged, and no truck, rack, leveller, wrapper or baler is returned to service until it is safe and recorded.

2. The Technician works under the direction of the Shift Supervisor on shift — mornings 06:00-14:00 or afternoons 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved by the Warehouse Manager. Work is prioritised with the Supervisor and Dispatchers to protect receiving at inbound Doors 1-4, staging at outbound Doors 5-8 and replenishment of Zone C, and handover is completed under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. The all-electric MHE fleet is maintained under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation: 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t for the high bays in Zone B, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks. The Technician supports the rule that every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day, reviews the checklists, grounds any truck with a brake, steering, fork, chain, light, horn, battery, charger or leak defect, and clears it only after repair and log entry.

4. Racking and storage equipment in the 6,000 m2 hall are maintained on a planned schedule. The 2,400-position high-bay racking in Zone B at 2,700 kg maximum per bay, ground-level pick faces and flow racks in the 1,200 m2 Zone C, and block stacking limited to 3 pallets high and 3.5 m are inspected, with a documented racking safety inspection every month. Damage, overload or instability is barriered off, reported to the Shift Supervisor, and repaired and re-inspected before reloading. The 900 kg maximum per pallet including load is enforced as the basis for all loading.

5. Dock, dispatch and site equipment are maintained across the 3,500 m2 fenced yard and Zones A to F. Each of the 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height has its own leveller, maintained with doors, seals, dock ramps and bumpers; the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D, the cardboard baler, and the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners are serviced and logged. Faults that block Doors 1-4 inbound or Doors 5-8 outbound are escalated immediately to the Shift Supervisor and Dispatcher for re-planning.

6. The Technician maintains Zone E and Zone F control equipment under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. This includes doors, seals, alarms and ventilation for the 300 m2 chilled store held at +2 °C to +6 °C with manual verification each shift, and the separate 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage limited to 3,000 kg and 3 full-weight pallets. On any cold-chain alarm, spill or evacuation the Technician secures equipment as directed by the Shift Supervisor and does not authorise re-entry until cleared.

7. Repair discipline and spares control apply to every job. Every repair is logged with date, equipment, fault, action, parts and sign-off, defects from daily checks and monthly racking inspections are tracked to closure, and damaged goods found during maintenance go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Write-offs up to 500 EUR are approved by the Shift Supervisor and above 750 EUR exclusively by the Warehouse Manager.

8. Safety, authority and reporting rules apply without exception under PR-10, PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse and PR-14 Emergency evacuation. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory on the warehouse floor, seat belts are worn when testing trucks while moving, and the 8 km/h limit inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed, with drivers kept in the marked waiting area and the 1.2 m physically separated walkways, 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles kept clear. The Technician operates trucks for test only if individually authorised by the Warehouse Manager, reports every incident, near-miss or spill to the Supervisor for review, supports daily cycle counts under PR-08, and attends quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point.

title: Common Rules and Training
text:
1. All staff report through a single operational line. Every role — inbound operators, forklift operators, pickers, returns and packing staff, stock controllers, the maintenance technician and floaters — reports on shift to the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor. The Shift Supervisors and the Dispatchers report to the Warehouse Manager, who is accountable for the whole site in Port Sellow, its operations, safety and inventory accuracy.

2. Shifts are fixed and cover is mandatory. The site runs two shifts, Monday to Friday: mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, with one Shift Supervisor always present and in charge. In peak season Saturday morning overtime may be added. Only the Warehouse Manager approves overtime, and no shift starts without handover completed under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. Authority limits apply to everyone without exception. The Warehouse Manager alone signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results, approves damaged-goods write-offs above 750 EUR, approves overtime and authorises new forklift operators. The Shift Supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 750 EUR, approves final disposition of inspected returns and reviews every incident report. The Dispatcher owns dock scheduling, door and time-slot assignment and release of outbound loads.

4. Personal protective equipment is mandatory on the warehouse floor in the 6,000 m2 hall and in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are required for everyone with no exceptions, including visitors and drivers where they are permitted. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, including during testing and maintenance moves.

5. No licence, no truck. No person operates the 9 counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, the 5 reach trucks rated at 2.0 t, the 11 electric pallet jacks or the 12 hand pallet jacks without individual authorisation by the Warehouse Manager. Every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, defects ground the truck until cleared by the Shift Supervisor and the maintenance technician, and every repair is logged.

6. Site traffic and pedestrian rules bind all roles under PR-10 and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Speed limits are 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard, and 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers, main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack aisles of 3.0 m are kept clear, drivers wait in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall, and inbound Doors 1-4 and outbound Doors 5-8 are used only as assigned by the Dispatcher.

7. Every employee is trained on the fifteen procedures relevant to their role and works only to the warehouse brief where documents differ. Induction on day one covers Zones A to F, goods flow from document check to dispatcher release, the 900 kg maximum per pallet, rack and stacking limits, chilled storage at +2 °C to +6 °C, the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage limited to 3,000 kg, and use of the 20 shared WMS scanners. Cold-chain handling follows PR-12, hazmat and spill response PR-13, damaged goods PR-09 with same-day quarantine, cycle counts and stocktaking PR-08 with no adjustment without a second count, and returns within 14 days under PR-07.

8. Safety, counts and drills are duties for all. Everyone attends the quarterly evacuation drill under PR-14 with roll call at the north fence assembly point before re-entry, supports daily cycle counts on the rotating schedule and the annual shutdown stocktake, takes part in the monthly racking safety inspection follow-up as directed, reports every incident, near-miss, spill, cold-chain alarm or rack damage to the Shift Supervisor for review, and completes PR-15 handover at end of shift. The 2 floaters cover absence but to the same standards, tasks and PPE as the role they cover.

title: Receiving Slots and Intake
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides inbound receiving through Doors 1-4, which are designated inbound only. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and shall not be used for intake. All unloading takes place in Zone A receiving (800 m2) at 1.2 m dock height with dedicated dock levellers.

2. Every inbound delivery requires a pre-booked time slot. The dispatcher assigns each carrier a specific door and time slot and owns the dock schedule. Carriers without a confirmed slot shall not be unloaded out of sequence.

3. Drivers report to the marked waiting area in the fenced yard (3,500 m2) and remain there for check-in. Drivers are not permitted in the hall or in Zone A during unloading, inspection or booking, except under escort for sealed-load verification where required.

4. Intake is performed in strict sequence in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving: (a) document check, (b) unloading, (c) count and inspection, (d) system booking in the WMS, (e) put-away to Zone B, E or F. No step shall be skipped or reordered.

5. No goods are unloaded until the paperwork has been checked. Inbound operators verify delivery note, purchase order reference, quantities, batch and expiry data where applicable, and transport condition before breaking the seal. Nothing moves past Zone A until this check is passed.

6. Following document acceptance, inbound operators unload, count and visually inspect all goods in Zone A. Any visible damage, shortage, overage, mis-labelling or temperature excursion is recorded at receipt and held for review before booking.

7. Only inspected goods are booked into the WMS. Only booked goods are released for put-away to bulk storage (Zone B), cold zone (Zone E) or services and control (Zone F). Unbooked or uninspected stock shall not be put away, replenished to pick faces, or picked for orders.

8. Standard handling is based on a maximum pallet weight of 900 kg including load. Contracted curtain-side trailers are planned at 33 floor positions up to 26,000 kg, equating to 28 full-weight pallets per trailer. Any overweight, over-height or unstable pallet will be held in Zone A for rework before booking.

9. Receiving is staffed by 6 inbound operators across two shifts, Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, under a shift supervisor in charge of the floor. In peak season Saturday morning overtime is available by prior agreement, approved only by the warehouse manager.

10. Yard and hall movements during intake comply with site speed limits: 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard, and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Pedestrians use the 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers; main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.

11. All mechanical handling uses electric equipment operated only by authorised operators: 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks for intake moves, each subject to a documented check before first use each day. Six inbound operators do not perform high-bay put-away; transfer to Zone B racking is handed to forklift and reach-truck operators.

12. The Client will be notified the same shift of any receipt discrepancy, damage found at inspection, or refusal to book. Booked receipts are visible in the WMS by end of shift, with receipt date, quantities booked, and Zone A hold details where applicable.

title: Dispatch Capacity and Release
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides outbound dispatch through Doors 5-8, which are designated outbound only. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and shall not be used for dispatch. All outbound staging takes place in Zone D dispatch (900 m2) in front of docks 5-8 at 1.2 m dock height with dedicated dock levellers.

2. Outbound capacity is committed at 4 trailer loads per door per shift across 4 outbound doors, equating to 16 trailer loads per shift. At the site standard of maximum 900 kg per pallet including load, this is 448 full-weight pallets per shift as the most that can be promised to clients.

3. Trailer planning is based on contracted curtain-side trailers carrying 26,000 kg on 33 floor positions, equating to 28 full-weight pallets per trailer. The delivery van is planned at 1,800 kg on 6 positions and carries two full-weight pallets only; any requirement above 1,800 kg per van load is routed by trailer.

4. All dispatch is performed in strict sequence in accordance with PR-05 Packing and labelling and PR-06 Outbound dispatch: (a) scanner-verified picking in Zone C, (b) labelling and transfer to Zone D, (c) wrapping, (d) staging by outbound door, (e) dispatcher release, (f) loading and sealing. No load is loaded without release.

5. Only wrapped, labelled pallets are permitted in Zone D. Every pallet is stretch-wrapped on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, labelled with delivery, consignee and handling data, and staged for its assigned outbound door. Unwrapped or unlabelled pallets shall not be staged or loaded.

6. Every outbound load requires dispatcher release. The 2 dispatchers book transport, assign each carrier a door and time slot, own the dock schedule, and release the load only when wrapping, labelling, quantity and door allocation are confirmed in the WMS.

7. Drivers report to the marked waiting area in the fenced yard (3,500 m2) and remain there until called to their assigned door. Drivers are not permitted in the hall or in Zone D during staging, release or loading, except under escort for sealed-load verification where required.

8. Loading is performed by authorised forklift operators using electric equipment only: 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts and electric pallet jacks, each subject to a documented check before first use each day. Every truck is loaded to its assigned door, checked against the release, and sealed before departure.

9. Dispatch is staffed across two shifts, Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, under a shift supervisor in charge of the floor. In peak season Saturday morning overtime is available by prior agreement, approved only by the warehouse manager.

10. Yard and hall movements during dispatch comply with site speed limits: 8 km/h inside the building, 12 km/h in the yard, and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Pedestrians use the 1.2 m walkways separated by yellow barriers; main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.

11. Overweight, over-height or unstable pallets will not be loaded. Any pallet exceeding 900 kg including load, or found damaged at wrapping or staging, is held in Zone D for rework and the Client is notified the same shift with re-planned load details.

12. Released and loaded shipments are confirmed in the WMS by end of shift, with door, trailer or van reference, pallet count, seal number, and departure time. Any short-load, carrier no-show or delayed release is notified to the Client the same shift with the next available door and slot.

title: Operating Hours and Cut-offs
text:
1. Standard operating hours are Monday to Friday in two shifts: mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00. All inbound receiving in Zone A and outbound dispatch in Zone D are staffed only within these shifts under one shift supervisor in charge of the floor.

2. Outside these hours the site is closed for routine intake and dispatch. No unloading at Doors 1-4 and no loading at Doors 5-8 takes place overnight, on Saturdays outside agreed overtime, or on Sundays, unless agreed as peak-season overtime.

3. In peak season Saturday morning overtime is available by prior agreement to extend intake and dispatch capacity. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime, and overtime slots are allocated by the dispatcher through the dock schedule once approved.

4. Committed throughput per shift is limited by outbound dock capacity: 4 outbound doors each handling 4 trailer loads per shift, equating to 16 trailer loads per shift. At the site standard of maximum 900 kg per pallet including load, this is 448 full-weight pallets per shift as the most that can be promised.

5. Inbound intake is planned within the same shift envelope and dock discipline. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and Doors 5-8 are outbound only, and every carrier is assigned a door and time slot by the dispatcher, who owns the dock schedule. Drivers wait in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard and never in the hall.

6. Trailer and van planning uses fixed standards for cut-off application: contracted curtain-side trailers at 26,000 kg on 33 floor positions, equating to 28 full-weight pallets per trailer, and the delivery van at 1,800 kg on 6 positions, carrying two full-weight pallets only. Loads above these standards are routed by trailer and counted against the 16-load per shift limit.

7. Cut-off times govern which shift a request belongs to. An inbound delivery is committed to its booked slot only if pre-booked with complete paperwork and arrival within its time window; documents are checked before unloading in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving, and late or undocumented arrivals are rescheduled to the next available slot.

8. An outbound order is committed to a shift's dispatch plan only if released with complete picking, wrapping and labelling data before that shift's order cut-off. The dispatcher releases loads in accordance with PR-06 Outbound dispatch only when wrapping, labelling, quantity and door allocation are confirmed; only wrapped, labelled pallets are permitted in Zone D.

9. Work not completed by end of shift is carried forward under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. The outgoing shift supervisor hands over staged loads in Zone D, held receipts in Zone A, door allocations and carrier status to the incoming shift, and the Client is notified the same shift of any short-load, delayed release or rescheduled receipt with the next available door and slot.

10. Booked receipts and released shipments are visible in the WMS by end of shift. Receiving is performed by 6 inbound operators, picking in Zone C against scanner tasks, and loading by authorised operators using electric equipment subject to a documented check before first use each day, within site speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

11. Cut-off times for each Client, including order cut-off, inbound pre-book cut-off and same-day change deadlines, are fixed in the Client schedule appendix and applied strictly against the limits above. Requests received after cut-off, or exceeding 448 full-weight pallets per shift or 16 trailer loads per shift, are automatically planned to the next shift with available capacity and confirmed to the Client by end of shift.

title: Picking and Packing Accuracy
text:
1. Picking is performed only in Zone C picking (1,200 m2) from ground-level pick faces and flow racks. No picking takes place from bulk storage in Zone B, from receiving in Zone A, or from quarantine or the hazmat cage in Zone F.

2. Pick faces are replenished from bulk storage before each picking shift in accordance with PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Replenishment moves only WMS-booked stock from Zone B to Zone C, confirmed by scanner, and no picking shift starts with unreplenished or unconfirmed faces.

3. All replenishment is executed by authorised forklift and reach-truck operators using electric equipment subject to a documented check before first use each day. Rack storage aisles of 3.0 m and main transport aisles of 4.0 m are observed, with site speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

4. Customer orders are picked only by 10 pickers working scanner tasks in Zone C under the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. Picking is staffed across two shifts, Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, with peak-season Saturday morning overtime only as approved by the warehouse manager.

5. Every pick is performed in strict sequence in accordance with PR-04 Order picking: (a) accept scanner task on the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners, (b) travel by the separated 1.2 m pedestrian walkways where on foot, (c) scan source location, (d) scan each item, (e) confirm quantity. No item is picked without an active WMS task.

6. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed. Any scan mismatch, short pick-face quantity, damaged unit, or batch and expiry mismatch stops the task, and the picker reports to the shift supervisor for recount or replenishment before completion. Unverified items shall not be packed, labelled or moved to Zone D.

7. Packing and labelling are performed in accordance with PR-05 Packing and labelling immediately after scan-verified picking. Goods are packed to protect packed consumer goods in transit, labelled with delivery, consignee, contents and handling data, and checked against the WMS order before transfer.

8. Standard unit of handling is a pallet of at most 900 kg including load. Overweight, over-height, unstable or damaged pallets or cartons are held and not transferred to dispatch. Damaged goods found during picking or packing go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found in accordance with PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

9. Only scan-verified, packed and labelled goods are moved to Zone D dispatch. Transfer is by authorised operators with electric and hand pallet equipment, and only wrapped, labelled pallets are permitted in Zone D for staging in front of Doors 5-8. Unwrapped, unlabelled or unverified stock shall not be staged or loaded.

10. Chilled and hazmat picks follow their zone rules without exception. Cold-chain picks from Zone E (300 m2, held at +2 °C to +6 °C) comply with PR-12 Cold-chain handling, and hazmat picks from the ventilated 60 m2 cage in Zone F comply with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for all floor work, with seat belts worn whenever a truck is moving.

11. Picking and packing completion is recorded in the WMS by end of shift. The outgoing shift hands over incomplete tasks, replenishment needs and held items under PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and the Client is notified the same shift of any short pick, held batch or order that cannot be completed as released.

title: Put-away and Storage Accuracy
text:
1. Put-away applies only to goods booked in the WMS following document check, unloading, counting and inspection in Zone A in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving. Unbooked, uninspected or held stock shall not be put away to Zone B, E or F, replenished to Zone C, or picked for orders.

2. All put-away is performed in strict sequence in accordance with PR-02 Put-away to storage: (a) confirm booked status and destination zone in the WMS, (b) scan pallet and target location, (c) transport by authorised equipment, (d) place and scan-verify location. No pallet is stored without an active WMS put-away task and location confirmation.

3. Bulk storage is provided in Zone B bulk storage (2,200 m2) with high-bay pallet racking of 2,400 pallet positions. Flow to Zone C picking is fed only from this booked bulk stock, with pick faces replenished before each picking shift in accordance with PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces.

4. Rack loading limits are absolute and planned on the site standard of maximum 900 kg per pallet including load. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, and any pallet exceeding 900 kg, over-height, unstable or damaged is held for rework and not placed in racking.

5. Free block-stacking outside racking is limited to 3 pallets high and 3.5 m height. Higher, heavier or unstable stacks shall not be built, and main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack storage aisles of 3.0 m are kept clear at all times.

6. Chilled goods are put away only to Zone E cold zone (300 m2), held between +2 °C and +6 °C in accordance with PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Cold-chain put-away is prioritised on arrival, with alarms and manual temperature verification each shift, and any temperature excursion at receipt is held in Zone A before booking.

7. Hazmat goods are stored only in the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F services and control, in accordance with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Hazmat never sits anywhere else, and no more than 3,000 kg is held at a time, equating to at most 3 full-weight pallets.

8. Put-away is executed only by authorised forklift operators using electric equipment subject to a documented check before first use each day in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. High-bay placement is performed only by reach trucks rated at 2.0 t, with general moves by 3.0 t counterbalance forklifts and electric and hand pallet jacks.

9. Storage accuracy is scan-verified at placement and owned day to day by 2 stock controllers. Every location error, damaged pallet, or quantity mismatch found during put-away stops the task for recount and correction before confirmation, and no adjustment is posted without a second count in accordance with PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

10. All floor work during put-away and storage complies with site safety rules in accordance with PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed, on separated routes with 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, with seat belts worn whenever a truck is moving.

11. Put-away completion and stored locations are visible in the WMS by end of shift. Incomplete put-away, held pallets and location corrections are handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and the Client is notified the same shift of any booked goods not available for replenishment or picking, with location and next action.

title: Cycle Counts, Stocktake and Reporting
text:
1. Inventory accuracy is owned day to day by 2 stock controllers in accordance with PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site and signs off the stocktake results, and no other sign-off replaces that approval.

2. Cycle counts run every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule covering Zones B, C, E and F. Counting is performed by stock controllers with scanner tasks on the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners, under the shift supervisor in charge of the floor, and counts never stop for outbound or replenishment activity.

3. Only WMS-booked stock is counted as available inventory. Goods held in Zone A awaiting inspection and booking, goods in quarantine in Zone F, and staged loads in Zone D are counted separately as held or staged and shall not be included in available stock figures reported to the Client.

4. Every count is performed in strict sequence in accordance with PR-08: (a) freeze and record the system quantity for the location, (b) physically count by scan-verification, (c) compare system to physical, (d) recount on any difference. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count.

5. Any difference confirmed by second count is recounted or investigated before adjustment, including check of recent put-away to Zone B, E or F, replenishment to Zone C, picking and packing activity, and returns inspection in Zone F. Location errors are corrected at the rack or pick face before the adjustment is confirmed in the WMS.

6. Once a year Harborwick 3PL shuts down for a full wall-to-wall stocktake of all zones.
