The stocktake is planned by the warehouse manager, executed across shifts by inbound operators, pickers, forklift operators and stock controllers, and personally signed off by the warehouse manager before system balances are reset.

7. Damaged goods found during any count go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found in accordance with PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Write-off above 750 EUR is signed off only by the warehouse manager; write-offs up to 750 EUR are approved by the shift supervisor, and no scrapped or adjusted stock is removed from the books without that approval.

8. Racking and storage condition found during counts is reported to the maintenance technician, who maintains trucks, racking and dock equipment and logs every repair. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month, and any bay found damaged or overloaded beyond 2,700 kg per bay or 900 kg per pallet is emptied and held until cleared.

9. All count activity complies with site safety rules. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, seat belts are worn whenever a truck is moving, and speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed on separated routes with 1.2 m walkways and 4.0 m main aisles.

10. Reporting is provided in the WMS by end of shift. Daily cycle-count results, second-count outcomes, adjustments posted, and held quantities are visible the same shift, and incomplete zones and follow-up recounts are handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

11. The Client is notified the same shift of any confirmed shortage, overage, batch or expiry correction affecting open orders, and receives a summary of cycle-count coverage with the annual stocktake report signed by the warehouse manager, including adjustments, quarantine movements and next actions for unresolved differences.

chapter_title: Damaged Goods, Returns and Chilled Storage
title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. handles all damaged goods in accordance with PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Any pallet, carton or unit found damaged, leaking, contaminated, crushed or otherwise unsaleable at receipt, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing, dispatch or counting is treated as damaged goods without exception.

2. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F services and control (600 m2) the same day they are found. The finder stops the task, secures the goods against further damage or movement, and reports to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor for transfer the same shift. No damaged stock remains in Zone A, B, C, D or E overnight.

3. Quarantine is physically segregated within Zone F, separate from returns inspection, value-added packing, and the ventilated 60 m2 hazmat cage. Only quarantined stock is held there, clearly labelled with date found, origin location, order or receipt reference, quantity and reason. Damaged hazmat is secured only in the hazmat cage in accordance with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, never in general quarantine.

4. All quarantine moves are performed in strict sequence: (a) identify and segregate at point of find, (b) scan or record out of available location, (c) transfer by authorised operators with electric or hand pallet equipment, (d) book into quarantine in the WMS as unavailable. Quarantined quantities are excluded from available stock and from pick-face replenishment and picking.

5. Every quarantine receipt is documented the same shift with photographs where the damage is visible, quantity affected, batch and expiry data, and suspected cause. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report arising from damaged goods, and the maintenance technician is notified where racking, MHE or dock equipment damage is involved and logs every repair.

6. Quarantined stock shall not be restocked, reworked, picked, packed or loaded without formal disposition. Returns and packing staff inspect quarantined goods in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap, supported by second count where quantity is in doubt in accordance with PR-08. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count.

7. Chilled goods found damaged are quarantined the same day under PR-09 with PR-12 Cold-chain handling observed. Temperature integrity is maintained until inspection, any excursion is recorded, and goods requiring +2 °C to +6 °C are not returned to Zone E cold zone (300 m2) without documented clearance.

8. Disposition and write-off approvals are fixed. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected goods and damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR. Any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR is signed off only by the warehouse manager, who is accountable for the whole site. No scrapped or adjusted stock is removed from the books without that approval.

9. Standard handling is based on a maximum pallet weight of 900 kg including load. Damaged pallets that are overweight, unstable or unsafe to lift are reworked or decanted in place before transfer, using equipment subject to a documented check before first use each day in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

10. All quarantine work complies with site safety rules in accordance with PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the floor, seat belts are worn whenever a truck is moving, and speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed on separated routes with 1.2 m walkways and 4.0 m main aisles.

11. Quarantine status is visible in the WMS by end of shift. Incomplete inspections, pending dispositions and approved write-offs are handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and the Client is notified the same shift of any damage affecting booked receipts or open orders, with quantities held, location in quarantine, proposed disposition and approval status.

chapter_title: Damaged Goods, Returns and Chilled Storage
title: Returns Inspection and Disposition
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. handles all customer returns in accordance with PR-07 Returns handling. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery only, counted from the recorded departure date in the WMS. Returns presented after 14 days, without delivery reference, or without prior Client authorisation shall not be accepted as returns.

2. All returns are received through the assigned inbound door and transferred to Zone F services and control (600 m2) for inspection. Drivers wait in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard and never in the hall, and no return is unloaded until paperwork is checked in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving.

3. Returns inspection takes place only in Zone F, separate from quarantine, value-added packing, and the ventilated 60 m2 hazmat cage. Goods remain on hold as unavailable stock until inspection is complete, and shall not be restocked to Zone B or E, replenished to Zone C, or picked for orders before disposition.

4. Every returned unit is inspected without exception. The 4 returns and packing staff check quantity, condition, seal and packaging integrity, labelling, batch and expiry data, and temperature history for chilled goods, and record each unit as restockable, reworkable or scrap. No bulk acceptance or sampling replaces unit-level inspection.

5. Inspection is performed in strict sequence: (a) confirm return authorisation and 14-day eligibility, (b) count and scan-verify against the delivery reference, (c) inspect every unit and photograph visible damage, (d) segregate by proposed outcome. Suspected quantity errors are resolved by second count, and no adjustment is ever posted without a second count in accordance with PR-08.

6. Returns staff propose restock, rework or scrap for every inspected line in Zone F. Restock is proposed only for sealed, undamaged, in-date goods in saleable condition; rework for goods requiring relabelling, repacking or decanting; scrap for damaged, contaminated, expired or otherwise unsaleable goods. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found in accordance with PR-09.

7. Final disposition is fixed. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Restock is booked back to available stock only after that approval; rework is released to value-added packing in Zone F; scrap is held in quarantine pending write-off approval.

8. Write-off approvals are fixed. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 750 EUR; any write-off above 750 EUR is signed off only by the warehouse manager, who is accountable for the whole site. No scrapped or adjusted stock is removed from the books without that approval.

9. Chilled and hazmat returns follow their zone rules without exception. Chilled returns are inspected under PR-12 Cold-chain handling with integrity maintained until clearance, and are not returned to Zone E cold zone (300 m2, +2 °C to +6 °C) without documented clearance. Hazmat returns are secured only in the hazmat cage in accordance with PR-13, never in general returns or quarantine, within the 3,000 kg limit.

10. All returns work complies with site safety rules in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Moves are by authorised operators with electric or hand pallet equipment subject to a documented check before first use each day. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, with seat belts worn whenever a truck is moving, and speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps observed on separated routes with 1.2 m walkways and 4.0 m main aisles.

11. Returns status is visible in the WMS by end of shift. Quantities received, inspected, restocked, sent to rework or held for scrap are recorded the same shift, pending dispositions are handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and the Client is notified the same shift of any return affecting available stock, with eligibility outcome, quantities, proposed and approved disposition, and approval status.

chapter_title: Damaged Goods, Returns and Chilled Storage
title: Temperature-Controlled Storage
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides chilled storage only in Zone E cold zone (300 m2), held between +2 °C and +6 °C at all times in accordance with PR-12 Cold-chain handling. No chilled goods are stored in Zone B, C, D, F or the yard, and ambient stock is never held in Zone E.

2. Cold-chain handling applies end to end: receipt in Zone A, put-away to Zone E, storage, replenishment and picking, packing, dispatch staging, returns and quarantine. Every chilled move is performed in strict sequence in accordance with PR-12: (a) verify temperature at point of handling, (b) minimise time outside controlled conditions, (c) scan-verify in the WMS, (d) restore to +2 °C to +6 °C without delay.

3. Inbound chilled goods are prioritised on arrival. Documents are checked before unloading in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving, then quantity, condition and temperature are inspected in Zone A. Any temperature excursion, visible damage or missing batch and expiry data is recorded at receipt and held in Zone A before booking; only inspected goods are booked.

4. Put-away to Zone E is immediate after booking in accordance with PR-02 Put-away to storage. Only WMS-booked chilled stock is put away, by authorised operators with electric equipment subject to a documented check before first use each day. Standard handling is based on a maximum pallet weight of 900 kg including load, and overweight, unstable or damaged pallets are reworked before placement.

5. Zone E is continuously monitored by calibrated alarms with a manual temperature verification each shift. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor ensures the manual check is completed mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, and during any approved Saturday morning overtime. Any reading outside +2 °C to +6 °C triggers immediate PR-12 response, segregation and Client notification the same shift.

6. Picking of chilled goods is scan-verified and time-controlled. Pick faces fed from Zone E are replenished before each picking shift in accordance with PR-03, picked only by 10 pickers on WMS scanner tasks in accordance with PR-04, and every picked item is scan-verified before packing in accordance with PR-05. Unverified, unlabelled or temperature-compromised units shall not be moved to Zone D.

7. Only wrapped, labelled chilled pallets are permitted in Zone D, staged for Doors 5-8 following dispatcher release in accordance with PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Cold-chain integrity is maintained through wrapping, staging, loading and sealing, and any excursion found at staging stops the load for inspection and re-decision.

8. Damaged chilled goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found in accordance with PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, with PR-12 observed. Temperature integrity is maintained until inspection, the excursion is recorded, and goods are not returned to Zone E without documented clearance. Returns staff propose restock, rework or scrap; the shift supervisor approves final disposition up to 750 EUR, and only the warehouse manager signs off write-offs above 750 EUR.

9. Chilled returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery only and inspected only in Zone F in accordance with PR-07 Returns handling. Integrity is maintained until clearance, every unit is inspected, and no chilled return is restocked to Zone E, replenished to pick faces or picked for orders before approved disposition with second count where quantity is in doubt in accordance with PR-08.

10. All chilled work complies with site safety rules in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the floor, seat belts are worn whenever a truck is moving, and speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 12 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed on separated routes with 1.2 m walkways and 4.0 m main aisles.

11. Chilled status is visible in the WMS by end of shift. Temperature logs, manual verifications, alarm events, quarantine movements and pending clearances are recorded the same shift and handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and the Client is notified the same shift of any excursion, held receipt, short pick or quarantined quantity, with location, quantities affected, proposed disposition and approval status.
